GROWTH DRIVERS OF THE INDUSTRY
We believe the following factors will drive the growth of the industry:
• Market Demand Expansion. The rapid growth of the renewable energy sector and the
increasing adoption of electric vehicles have substantially heightened the demand for
lead-acid batteries and copper, thereby propelling the growth of these industries. The
ongoing development of new infrastructure, including ultra-high voltage transmission
systems, 5G communication networks, and electrified railways, alongside the increasing
demand for photovoltaic supports within the renewable energy sector, continues to drive a
steady rise in the demand for zinc. Details of such market demand for zinc, lead and copper
are set out as follows:
(i) zinc concentrates: According to the zinc industry chain, zinc concentrates are
ultimately used in sectors such as infrastructure, construction, transportation,
consumer durables, and machinery. The infrastructure sector accounts for the largest
share in China’s downstream zinc end-use, representing over 30%, and both
traditional and new infrastructure boost demand for zinc ingots. In traditional
infrastructure, areas such as transportation infrastructure, urban-rural cold chain and
other logistics infrastructure, municipal and industrial park infrastructure will all
bolster zinc demand. For new infrastructure, sectors like 5G telecom base stations,
ultra-high voltage power transmission, intercity high-speed rail, and urban rail transit
also have substantial demand for galvanized structural components, so the push in
infrastructure may effectively drive zinc demand. With the accelerated advancement
of new energy, the PV sector is experiencing high growth. Zinc consumption in PV
is approximately 1,800 t/GW, which will also drive zinc consumption. In the wind
− 108 −

=== PAGE 119 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
power industry, zinc is mainly used in wind turbine towers and bolts, with each GW
of wind power installation requiring 5,500 t of zinc. With the rapid development of
offshore and onshore wind power, demand for zinc is expected to continue increasing.
(ii) lead concentrates:According to the lead industry chain, the main end-use application
of lead concentrates is lead-acid batteries. Lead-acid batteries dominate in low-speed
EVs and e-bikes. After China implemented the e-bike trade-in policy in September
2024, cumulative e-bike replacements under the trade-in program reached 1.38
million units from September to December 2024, directly boosting lead-acid battery
demand and thereby driving lead concentrate consumption. In the energy storage
system sector, breakthroughs in lead-carbon battery technology (such as Kungong
Technology’s aluminum-based lead-carbon battery) have addressed the shortcomings
of traditional lead-acid batteries, improving safety performance by 2-3 orders of
magnitude compared to lithium batteries, and have been applied in projects like
Guangzhou Huachu and Gansu Zhongdian. Demand for lead-acid batteries in areas
such as backup power for telecom base stations and marine starter batteries will also
remain stable.
(iii) copper concentrates: According to the copper industry chain, the main end-use
applications of copper concentrates include power, construction, transportation,
consumer durables, and machinery. Demand from the power sector is the core driver
of copper consumption growth, accounting for about 45% of China’s total copper
consumption in 2024, with copper products such as power cables, distributors, and
transformers widely used in power investments. The “National Power 14th Five-Year
Overall Plan and 2035 Vision Outlook” indicates that China’s power structure will
shift from traditional fossil fuels to clean, low-carbon renewable energy power, with
nearly 6 trillion yuan invested in the power grid and related industries; according to
the “New-Type Power System Action Plan 2021-2030,” smart flexible distribution
networks, digital grids,AC-DC hybrid grids, smart distribution stations, and ESS will
become major directions for power sector development, which will directly drive
copper demand. Copper consumption in the transportation sector is mainly
concentrated in the production of traditional automobiles and NEVs, as well as the
construction of new energy charging infrastructure (represented by charging piles).
NEVs, benefiting from the continuous expansion of market size, continue to promote
copper consumption. In addition, the widespread deployment of charging piles will
also boost copper consumption in the later market.
• Policies Support. According to the Management Measures for Green Mine Construction in
the Xizang Autonomous Region (西藏自治區綠色礦山建設管理辦法) mining enterprises
included in the green mine directory are entitled to the following support policies:
(i) Mineral Resource Policy Support: For mining indicators of mineral types subject to
total quantity control and the allocation of mining rights that comply with national
industrial policies, priority will be given to green mining enterprises.
− 109 −

=== PAGE 120 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
(ii) Land UseAssurance for Green Mine Construction: When formulating the overall land
use plan, the land required for green mine construction projects will be integrated into
the planning arrangements, and priority will be given in the annual land use plan to
meet the reasonable demand for newly constructed or expanded green mines.
(iii) Financial and Tax Policy Support: Enterprises engaged in the research, development,
and transformation of technologies for green mine construction within the scope of
“National Key Supported High-Tech Fields” that meet the criteria for recognition as
high-tech enterprises may benefit from a reduced corporate income tax rate of 15%.
Furthermore, green mining enterprises will be exempt from resource taxes on the
extraction of associated minerals and tailings; resource tax reductions of 50% will
apply to the extraction of low-grade minerals.
(iv) Other National Support Policies for Green Mine Construction: In addition to the
aforementioned benefits, being included in the national green mine directory is a
significant achievement for our Company in realising its green development goals. It
also serves as an important means for us to fulfil its social responsibilities, enhance
industry self-discipline, and ensure the healthy development of the mining sector.
This recognition greatly contributes to the enhancement of our brand value and
sustainable development, yielding substantial economic and social benefits.
Furthermore, the implementation of the trade-in policy is expected to stimulate the
consumption of downstream products containing lead, zinc and copper, thereby
indirectly benefiting the sales of our refined products.
The trade-in policy refers to the state’s use of fiscal subsidies, tax incentives,
financial support, and other means to encourage consumers to retire old consumer
goods or production equipment, such as home appliances, automobiles, agricultural
machinery, and construction machinery, and purchase new products that meet higher
energy efficiency, more environmentally friendly, and smarter standards, thereby
boosting domestic demand, promoting industrial upgrading, and reducing
environmental pollution. For example, in the automotive sector, consumers can
receive a certain amount of subsidy for retiring old internal combustion engine
vehicles or new energy vehicles and purchasing new ones; in the home appliance
sector, purchasing green, smart home appliances with top energy efficiency ratings
also qualifies for subsidies or discounts.
The trade-in policy has directly increased sales of products such as automobiles,
machinery, home appliances, and 3C devices, which require various non-ferrous
metals in their production. This has promoted the growth of end-use consumption of
non-ferrous metals such as lead, zinc, and copper, thereby driving upstream metal
mining.

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
• Technological Innovation. The industry is characterised by ongoing technological
advancements that enhance resource extraction efficiency and utilisation, mitigate
environmental impacts, and promote sustainable practices.
• Infrastructure Investment. The escalation of investments in infrastructure, particularly in
power grid modernisation and urban rail transit systems, serves to stimulate demand for
copper and its associated products.
• Environmental and Green Development Trends. Increasingly stringent environmental
policies are leading to the consolidation of the industry by phasing out smaller enterprises,
thereby providing larger firms with expanded market opportunities and fostering the green
transformation of the sector.
DEVELOPMENT TREND OF THE INDUSTRY
The following are some of the trends of the global and PRC zinc, lead and copper mining
industry:
• Green and Low-Carbon Transition. The zinc, lead and copper mining industry actively
practices the concept of green development by applying advanced environmental protection
technologies to reduce pollutant emissions and minimise environmental impact.
Technologies such as waste heat recovery and energy-saving equipment are promoted to
improve energy utilisation efficiency and reduce carbon emissions.
• Development of Intelligence and Automation. Intelligent technologies are widely applied in
mining, such as unmanned vehicles and automated tunnelling equipment, to enhance
production efficiency and safety. The Internet of Things and big data technologies are used
to monitor the mining environment and equipment operation status in real time, providing
early risk warnings to ensure safe mine operations. In the future, data-driven intelligent
management models will continue to advance, enhancing the overall competitiveness of the
industry.
• Resource Integration and Technological Innovation. Enterprises integrate resources
through mergers and acquisitions to expand production scale and enhance market
competitiveness. Meanwhile, breakthroughs in the development and utilisation
technologies for low-grade and refractory ores have improved the comprehensive
utilisation rate of resources. It is economically and practically beneficial to recover value
from low-grade and refractory ores. Advances in resource exploration technologies also
provide a strong support for industry development, helping enterprises discover more
potential mineral resources.

=== PAGE 122 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
ENTRY BARRIERS OF THE INDUSTRY
Both the global and PRC nonferrous industries have high entry barriers, including:
• Resource Barriers. Ore reserves and resource quantities are key factors for the sustainable
development of mining companies. Due to different formation conditions, the types,
grades, and orebody occurrence conditions of nonferrous metals vary significantly across
mines, greatly impacting the production costs of nonferrous metal mining companies.
Acquiring nonferrous metal resources of a certain scale and mining value is the primary
barrier to entering the industry in which our Company operates.
• Technical Barriers. With the decline in ore grades and the increase in mining depth, the
difficulty and complexity of mining operations have correspondingly risen, creating high
technical barriers for new entrants. Exploration and mining of existing, newly built, rebuilt,
and expanded mines require the latest technologies, complete sets of equipment, and
supporting facilities. Furthermore, only companies equipped with advanced technologies
and sufficient experience can meet the increasingly stringent government requirements for
safety production and environmental protection, thereby increasing the difficulty for new
entrants.
• Talent Barriers. The nonferrous metal mining industry requires professional talent for
various stages such as mining and ore processing. Recruiting and training professionals
with strong expertise to form a technical team requires a long cycle, making it difficult for
new entrants to address the lack of talent in a short period.
• Capital Barriers. The nonferrous metal mining industry is a capital-intensive sector. First,
geological exploration during the prospecting phase requires significant investment, with
uncertainty regarding whether resources can be discovered. Second, in addition to the fixed
investments required for nonferrous metal mining facilities, company’s construction
involves the development of supporting infrastructure such as transportation, water, and
electricity, as well as investments in related auxiliary facilities for environmental
protection and safety, resulting in substantial overall project investment, forming a
significant capital barrier. Moreover, as the government imposes increasingly stringent
requirements for safety production and environmental protection, investments in these
areas will also increase, leading to additional expenditures.
• Policy Barriers. China implements strict administrative licensing systems for the
development and production of nonferrous metal mines. According to the regulations,
enterprises must obtain an “Exploration Licence” for nonferrous metal resource exploration
and “Mining Licence”, “Safety Production Licence”, and other permits for nonferrous
metal mining. For operations involving explosives, a “Blasting Operation Unit Licence”
and other relevant permits are required. If the mining area involves the use of surface or
underground water resources, or the occupation of grassland or forest resources, approval
from relevant departments or the acquisition of corresponding qualifications is necessary,
or fees must be paid as stipulated. National and local policies and regulations also establish
− 112 −

=== PAGE 123 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
standards for production scale, process equipment, safety assurance, environmental
protection implementation, and production layout in nonferrous metal mining. For
instance, the minimum production scale for newly established lead-zinc mines must not be
less than 30.0 kt per year for a single mine.
LIMITATIONS ON THE FUTURE DEVELOPMENT OF RECYCLED PRODUCTS
• Product Quality. Recycled Products face challenges in achieving the precision standards
required by high-value manufacturing industries such as aerospace, national defence and
precision electronics due to the complex sourcing of raw materials (e.g., dismantling of
scrap from various downstream industries).
• Supply Stability. The capacity of Recycled Products is highly dependent on the stability of
the scrap product recycling system. Currently, the uneven regional distribution of recycling
companies and regulatory policies contribute to instability in raw material supply. The
capacity utilisation rates of recycled lead producers are limited due to raw material supply
constraints, including the tight availability of waste lead-acid batteries and environmental
protection regulations, which restrict the stability of recycled lead supply. Meanwhile, the
recycled zinc industry remains in a developmental stage and faces significant constraints
that limit its current scale and growth potential. In contrast, primary products
(lead/zinc/copper concentrates) benefit from a globalised mineral supply chain, ensuring
stable production for downstream industries.
• Product Price. The cost of Recycled Products has approached that of primary products
(zinc, lead and copper concentrates) due to the impact of environmental regulations,
particularly in terms of investments in environmental protection equipment (such as
exhaust gas treatment) and the costs associated with purification technologies.
Consequently, the price advantage of Recycled Products has significantly diminished.
• Technical Adaptation Barriers. Some downstream clients in certain industries have
production lines that are deeply adapted to the parameters of primary products
(lead/zinc/copper concentrates). Switching to recycled raw materials would require the
replacement of production lines and equipment, incurring substantial transformation costs.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
We are subject to a variety of PRC laws, rules and regulations affecting many aspects of our
business. This section summarises the major PRC laws and regulations that may have a significant
impact on our business and operations in the PRC.
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO MINERAL RESOURCES
The Mineral Resources Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國礦產資源法》) was promulgated by
the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (“SCNPC”) on 19 March 1986 and became
effective on 1 October 1986. The SCNPC amended the Mineral Resources Law on 29 August 1996,
27 August 2009 and 8 November 2024, respectively. On 26 March 1994, the State Council
promulgated the Implementation Rules for the Mineral Resources Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和
國礦產資源法實施細則》) (“Implementation Rules”). The Mineral Resources Law of the PRC and its
Implementation Rules provide that:
• All mineral resources of the PRC, including such resources on the earth’s surface or
underground, are owned by the State. The State ownership of mineral resources shall
remain unchanged notwithstanding that the ownership or the right to use the land to which
such mineral resources are attached has been granted to a different entity or individual.The
State Council exercises the rights of ownership of the State in relation to mineral resources.
• The State protects the rational development and use of mineral resources and prohibits any
organisation or individual from using any means to seize or damage mineral resources.
• The exploration for and mining of mineral resources is subject to separate applications in
accordance with the law. A party must carry out registration procedures after the approval
of its application and the issue of exploration rights or mining rights. This does not apply,
however, if a mining enterprise which has already applied and obtained mining rights in
accordance with the law carries out exploration for the purpose of its own production
operations within the boundaries of its designated mining area. Those engaging in the
exploration and mining of mineral resources must comply with the stipulated qualification
conditions.
• The State implements a system of the paid acquisition of the issue of exploration rights and
mining rights. However, the State may, depending on circumstances, stipulate the
reductions in or exemptions from fee payments for these exploration rights and mining
rights be granted.
• The transfer of exploration rights and mining rights is prohibited, except in the following
instances: (i) the holder of exploration rights to a designated exploration area has the right
to undertake stipulated exploration work within that area and is then entitled to obtain in
priority mining rights to mine within the designated exploration area.After completing the
stipulated minimum amount of exploration operations, the holder of exploration rights may,
subject to approval in accordance with the law, transfer the exploration rights to another
party; (ii) a mining enterprise which has already obtained mining rights and which requires
to alter the holder of the mining rights due to an enterprise merger or division, or as the
− 115 −

=== PAGE 126 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
result of it entering a joint equity or cooperative venture with another party, or due to the
sale of enterprise assets, or other changes which alter ownership of enterprise assets, may
transfer the exploration rights to another party, subject to approval in accordance with the
law. The reselling of exploration rights and mining rights for profit is prohibited.
• The State Council department in charge of geology and mineral resources or the relevant
competent departments authorised by the State Council and the provincial, autonomous
regional or directly administered municipal people’s government departments in charge of
geology and mineral resources are responsible for the granting of exploration and mining
licences. Generally, holders of exploration licences and mining licences have those rights
and obligations as prescribed by laws.
Rights and Obligations of Holders of Exploration Licences
According to the Implementation Rules, the rights exercisable by a holder of an exploration
permit include, among other things, the following: (i) to conduct exploration according to the areas,
duration and targets stipulated in the exploration permit; (ii) to install power supply lines, water
supply pipelines and telecommunications lines in exploration areas and adjacent areas, but these shall
not affect or damage existing water pipelines or supply facilities or communication lines; (iii) to visit
exploration areas and adjacent areas; (iv) to use land temporarily according to project requirements;
(v) priority in obtaining the right to explore newly discovered types of minerals and mine mineral
resources within the exploration area; (vi) to sell mineral products recovered during exploration
according to the approved project; however, mineral products to be purchased on a monopoly basis
by units designated by the State Council shall be so purchased.
The obligations of a holder of an exploration permit include, among other things, the following:
(i) to commence construction within the prescribed time limit and complete exploration work within
the time limit stipulated in the exploration permit; (ii) to report on such matters as commencement of
operations to the exploration registration authority; (iii) to carry out construction according to the
exploration project design and not conduct the mining of mineral resources without authorisation; (iv)
when locating key minerals, to conduct comprehensive exploration and evaluation of associated
mineral resources; (v) to prepare a report on the exploration of mineral resources to be submitted to
the relevant departments for examination and approval; (vi) to collect archive materials on the results
of exploration of mineral resources for submission pursuant to relevant State regulations; (vii) to
comply with the provisions of laws and statutory regulations with regard to production safety,
restoration and reutilisation of land and environmental protection; (viii) to promptly seal or fill a mine
or hole left after completion of exploration for mineral resources or adopt other measures to eliminate
hidden dangers to safety.
Pursuant to the Administrative Measures on Registration of Blocks for Exploration of Mineral
Resources 《( 礦產資源勘查區塊登記管理辦法》) which became effective on 12 February 1998 and
was amended on 29 July 2014, the holder of an exploration permit shall meet the following minimum
exploration investment requirement from the date of obtaining the exploration permit: (i) RMB 2,000
per square kilometre for the first exploration year; (ii) RMB 5,000 per square kilometre for the second
exploration year; and (iii) RMB 10,000 per square kilometre for each exploration year from the third
exploration year.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Establishment of mine geological environment treatment and restoration fund account
According to “Notice on the Issuance of the Measures for the Administration of the Mine
Geological Environment Treatment and Restoration Fund (Trial)” 《( 西藏自治區礦山地質環境治理恢
復基金管理辦法(試行)》) jointly issued in 2020 by the Department of Natural Resources, Department
of Finance, and Department of Ecology and Environment of Xizang, mining companies in the PRC are
required to prepare a geological environmental protection and reclamation plan and to submit such
plan for assessment and approval by the relevant authorities. Furthermore, mining companies must
establish a mine geological environment treatment and restoration fund account in accordance with
the principles of “enterprise establishment, government supervision, demand assurance, and dedicated
use of funds.”
The fund is to be used exclusively for mine geological environment treatment, restoration, and
land reclamation. Mining companies are required to extract and use the fund according to a
pre-approved plan, and the extraction and use of the fund are subject to credit management by the
authorities. In accordance with applicable accounting standards, the anticipated disposal costs related
to the fund are included in the relevant asset costs and are extracted annually from the sales revenue
of mineral products over the expected mining period, and are accounted for as production costs.
Rights and Obligations of Holders of Mining Licences
According to the Implementation Rules, the rights exercisable by a holder of a mining permit
include, among other things, the following: (i) to conduct mining activities in accordance with the
mining scope and duration as stipulated in the mining permit; (ii) to sell mineral products, except
those mineral products to be purchased on a monopoly basis by units designated by the State Council;
(iii) to construct facilities for production subsistence within the mining areas as required for mining;
(iv) to legally obtain land use rights in accordance with production and construction requirements.
The obligations of a holder of a mining permit include, among other things, the following: (i)
to carry out construction or mining of mines within the approved time limit; (ii) to conduct effective
protection, rational mining, and comprehensive utilisation of mineral resources; (iii) to pay resource
tax and mineral resource royalty fees in accordance with the law; (iv) to comply with the provisions
of relevant laws and statutory regulations concerning safety in production, water and soil
conservation, land restoration and reutilisation and environmental protection; (v) to accept
supervision and administration of the department in charge of geology and mineral resources and the
relevant departments in charge, and to compile a ore reserve form and submit a statistical report on
the development and utilisation of mineral resources pursuant to regulations.
Comprehensive Mining and Utilisation
According to The Mineral Resources Law of the PRC, the exploitation of mineral resources shall
be conducted in accordance with reasonable mining sequences and methods, while effective measures
shall be taken to ensure that the mining recovery rate, mineral processing recovery rate, and
comprehensive utilisation rate meet the requirements of relevant national standards.
− 117 −

=== PAGE 128 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
In parallel with the exploitation of the main minerals, the minerals with industrial value that
occur in association or as by-products of the ordinary mineral production should be subject to unified
planning, comprehensive mining, and integrated utilisation to prevent waste. For minerals that cannot
be comprehensively exploited at the moment or must be extracted simultaneously but cannot be
comprehensively utilised for the time being, as well as tailings containing useful components,
effective protective measures shall be taken to prevent loss and damage.
In accordance with Specifications for Lead and Zinc Industry 《( 鉛鋅行業規範條件》), which
was issued by the MIIT on 28 February 2020 and came into effect on the same day, for underground
mining of lead-zinc ores, the comprehensive energy consumption per ton of raw ore must be below
4.4 kg of standard coal. For open-pit mining, the comprehensive energy consumption per ton of
extracted ore must be below 0.6 kg of standard coal. The comprehensive energy consumption for
lead-zinc ore beneficiation must be below 6.1 kg of standard coal per ton of ore. The mining recovery
rate, mineral processing recovery rate, and comprehensive utilisation rate of lead-zinc mining
enterprises shall comply with the relevant requirements stipulated in the Announcement on the
Minimum ‘Three Rates’ Indicators for the Rational Utilisation of Iron, Copper, Lead, Zinc, Rare
Earth, Potash and Fluorite Mineral Resources (Trial) 《( 關於鐵、銅、鉛、鋅、稀土、鉀鹽和螢石等
礦產資源合理開發利用“三率”最低指標要求 (試行) 的公告》) issued by the former Ministry of Land
and Resources.
Usage Fees and Renewal of Exploration and Mining Licences
Holders of exploration licences and holders of mining licences are subject to exploration right
usage fees and mining right usage fees, respectively. In accordance with theAdministrative Measures
on Registration of Blocks for Exploration of Mineral Resources, exploration right usage fees shall be
calculated according to the terms of the exploration permit and shall be payable on an annual basis.
The rate of exploration right usage fee for the first year to the third year of exploration shall be
RMB100 per square kilometre of exploration area per year. From the fourth year of exploration
onwards, the rate will be increased by RMB100 per square kilometre of exploration area per year.
However, the annual maximum rate shall not exceed RMB500 per square kilometre of exploration
area. According to the Administrative Measures for Registration of the Mining of Mineral Resources
(《礦產資源開採登記管理辦法》), which became effective on 12 February 1998 and amended on 29
July 2014, the mining right usage fee shall be paid on an annual basis. The rate of mining right usage
fee shall be RMB1,000 per square kilometre of mining area per year.
According to the Administrative Measures on Registration of Blocks for Exploration of Mineral
Resources, the maximum validity period of an exploration license is 3 years. The exploration rights
holder shall apply for renewal with the registration authority 30 days before the expiration of the
exploration license. Each extension shall not exceed two years. If the exploration rights holder fails
to apply for renewal within the specified period, the exploration license shall automatically become
void. Pursuant to the Administrative Measures for Registration of the Mining of Mineral Resources,
the validity period of a mining licence shall be determined according to the scale of the mine. The
maximum validity period of the initial term of a mining licence for a big-scale mine, medium-scale
mine and small-scale mine shall be 30 years, 20 years and 10 years, respectively. The mining licence
can be renewed within 30 days prior to its expiration, upon compliance with the prescribed extension
procedure. If the holder of a mining licence fails to renew its licence in time, such mining licence shall
be automatically annulled upon expiration.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Mining Right Transfer Proceeds
According to the Mining Right Transfer Proceeds Collection Measures 《( 礦業權出讓收益徵收
辦法》), which was promulgated by the MOF, MNR and STA on 24 March 2023 and became effective
on 1 May 2023, mining right holders shall pay mining right transfer proceeds. From 1 July 2017 to
30April 2023, any unpaid mining right transfer proceeds shall be calculated based on the mining right
transfer yield rate specified in these Measures and the sales revenue during the unpaid period. The
payable amount may be collected either in a lump sum or evenly over six years.
Related Resource Tax and Resource Compensation Fee
According to the Resource Tax Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國資源稅法》), which was
promulgated by the SCNPC on 26 August 2019 and became effective on 1 September 2020, the
specific rate of resource tax applicable to taxable products shall be governed by the List of Taxable
Items attached to the Resource Tax Law of the PRC, and the resource tax rate for lead ores, zinc ores
and copper ores (including raw ores and processed ores) shall be 2%-10%.
Pursuant to the Rules for the Administration of Collection of Mineral Resource Compensation
Fees 《( 礦產資源補償費徵收管理規定》), promulgated by the State Council on 27 February 1994 and
amended on 3 July 1997, the holder of a mining permit shall pay the mineral resource compensation
fees from sale proceeds of mineral products on a pro rata basis.
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION
The PRC Government has formulated a comprehensive set of environmental protection laws and
regulations that cover areas such as sewage discharge and waste disposal. The PRC laws and
regulations relating to environmental protection mainly include: the Environmental Protection Law of
the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國環境保護法》) (revised on 24 April 2014 and implemented on 1 January
2015), the Water Pollution Prevention and Control Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國水污染防治
法》) (revised on 27 June 2017 and implemented on 1 January 2018), the Atmospheric Pollution
Prevention and Control Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國大氣污染防治法》) (revised and
implemented on 26 October 2018), the Law of the PRC on Prevention and Control of Environmental
Pollution by Solid Waste 《( 中華人民共和國固體廢物污染環境防治法》) (revised on 29 April 2020
and implemented on 1 September 2020), the Environmental Protection Tax Law of the PRC 《( 中華
人民共和國環境保護稅法》) (revised and implemented on 26 October 2018), the Implementation
Regulation on the Environmental Protection Tax Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國環境保護稅法實
施條例》) (revised on 25 December 2017 and implemented on 1 January 2018), the Measures for
Pollutant Discharge Permitting Administration 《( 排淤許可管理辦法》) (promulgated on 1 April 2024
and implemented on 1 July 2024), the Law of the PRC on Noise Pollution Prevention and
Control 《( 中華人民共和國噪聲污染防治法》) (promulgated on 24 December 2021 and implemented
on 5 June 2022), and Provisions for the Protection of Geological Environment in Mines 《( 礦山地質
環境保護規定》) (revised and implemented on 24 July 2019).
Pursuant to the aforesaid laws and regulations, enterprises that discharge and dispose of toxic
and dangerous substances such as wastewater, waste gas and solid wastes shall comply with the
national and local standards of usage and shall declare to and register with the relevant environmental
protection administration authorities and pay pollution discharge fees according to law where
applicable.

Pursuant to the Law on Environmental ImpactAssessment of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國環境影

November 2017 and the Regulations on the Administration Construction Project Environmental
Protection 《( 建設項目環境保護管理條例》), which was revised on 16 July 2017 and implemented on
1 October 2017, after the completion of a construction project for which an environmental impact
report or an environmental impact report form is required, the construction entity shall, according to
standards and procedures prescribed by the environmental protection administrative authorities,
conduct environmental protection completion acceptance check and compile an acceptance check
report. A construction project for which an environmental impact report or an environmental impact
report form is required shall not be put into production or use until the environmental protection
completion acceptance check has been passed.
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO LAND
Pursuant to the Land Administration Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國土地管理法》), which
was promulgated on 25 June 1986 and was revised on 29 December 1988, 29August 1998, 28August
2004 and 26 August 2019, respectively, and the Regulations on the Implementation of the Land
Administration Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國土地管理法實施條例》), which was promulgated
on 27 December 1998 and was revised on 8 January 2011, 29 July 2014 and 2 July 2021,respectively,
land in the PRC is either state-owned or collectively-owned. State-owned land and collectively-owned
land may be allocated to units or individuals for use according to law. Lawfully registered land
ownership and land use rights are protected by law. In the case of temporary use of state-owned land
or collectively-owned land for construction projects or geological survey, approval shall be obtained
from the land administrative department of the government at or above the county level. Land users
shall sign contracts with relevant land administrative department or rural economic collective
organisations or village committees for the temporary use of land, depending on the ownership of land
and shall pay land compensation fees as stipulated in the contracts for the temporary use of land. The
term for the temporary use of land shall generally not exceed two years. The state shall establish a
territorial spatial planning system, and territorial spatial plans approved in accordance with the law
shall be the primary basis for various activities of land development, protection, and construction.
Where a territorial spatial plan has been worked out, the comprehensive plan for land utilisation and
the urban-rural plan shall no longer be effective. Before a territorial spatial plan is determined, the
existing overall plan for land utilisation and urban-rural plan legally approved shall continue to be
effective. The results of land surveys are of great importance in the preparation of territorial spatial
plans, as well as the management, protection and utilisation of natural resources.
− 120 −

=== PAGE 131 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Pursuant to the Mineral Resources Law of the PRC and the Measures for the Administration of
the Examination and Approval of the Use of Woodlands by Construction Projects 《( 建設項目使用林
地審核審批管理辦法》), which was promulgated on 31 March 2015 and was amended on 22
September 2016, in mining mineral resources, a mining enterprise or individual must observe the legal
provisions on environmental protection to prevent pollution of the environment. In mining mineral
resources, a mining enterprise or individual must economise on the use of land. In construction
projects occupying forest land, the forest land shall be used in a reasonable, economical, and intensive
manner in accordance with the protection and use plan. In case cultivated land, grassland or forest
land is damaged due to mining, the mining enterprise concerned shall take measures to utilise the land
affected, such as by reclamation, tree and grass planting, as appropriate to the local conditions.
Anyone who, in mining mineral resources, causes losses to the production and well-being of other
persons shall be liable for compensation and shall adopt necessary remedial measures.
Pursuant to the Regulation on Land Reclamation 《( 土地復墾條例》) which was promulgated and
came into effect on 5 March 2011 and the Measures for the Implementation of the Regulation on Land
Reclamation 《( 土地復墾條例實施辦法》), which came into effect on 1 March 2013 and was amended
on 24 July 2019, the production and construction entities or individuals shall be responsible for the
reclamation of the land destroyed by their production and construction activities. A land user shall,
when handling the application for a piece of construction land or handling the application for the
mining right, submit the plan for land reclamation for approval. Where the plan for land reclamation
does not meet the relevant requirements, the construction land use right or the mining permit cannot
be obtained. If a land user implements land reclamation in accordance with the land reclamation plan,
he shall report to the competent land and resources authorities of the local people’s governments at
or above the county level for examination and acceptance.
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO PRODUCTION SAFETY
The PRC Government has formulated a relatively comprehensive set of laws and regulations on
production safety, including the Work Safety Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國安全生產法》)
(effective as at 1 November 2002 and revised on 27 August 2009, 31 August 2014 and 10 June 2021,
respectively), the Mine Safety Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國礦山安全法》) (effective as at 1 May
1993 and revised on 27 August 2009) as well as the Regulations for the Implementation of the Mine
Safety Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國礦山安全法實施條例》) (effective as at 30 October 1996),
covering mineral resources exploration, mining and mine construction. The PRC Government applies
a work safety licensing system for production safety to mining enterprises under the Regulations on
Work Safety Licences 《( 安全生產許可證條例》) (effective as at 13 January 2004 and revised on 18
July 2013 and 29 July 2014, respectively). No mining enterprise may engage in production activities
without holding a valid work safety licence. Any mining enterprise which fails to satisfy the
production safety conditions set out in the Regulations on Work Safety Licences may not obtain a
work safety licence and carry out any production activity. Mining enterprises which have obtained the
work safety licences shall not lower their production safety standards, and shall be subject to the
supervision and inspection by the licensing authorities from time to time. If the licensing authority
is of the opinion that any of such enterprises no longer satisfy the production safety requirements, the
work safety licence may be withheld or revoked. The valid period for a work safety licence shall be
3 years. The enterprise may apply for extension of the licence within 3 months prior to expiration of
the licence, and if the licensed enterprise has been strictly complied with the relevant laws and
regulations in relation to work safety and free of any fatal accident during the term of the licence, with
− 121 −

=== PAGE 132 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
the consent of the licensing authority, the licence could be renewed without examination procedure.
The primary person in charge and the work safety management personnel of a mining enterprise shall
pass the assessment on their work safety knowledge and management capabilities conducted by the
competent work safety authority.
The PRC Government has also formulated a set of national standards on production safety for
the mining industry. For example, the mine design shall comply with production safety requirements
and industry practice; mining enterprises must establish and improve the safe production
responsibility system. Managers of mines shall be responsible for the safe production in their
respective enterprises. Mining enterprises must provide safety education and training to their workers
and staff; those without receiving safety education and training may not take up a post of duty.
Pursuant to the relevant requirements of the Mine Safety Law of the PRC, the Regulations on
the Reporting, Investigation and Disposition of Work SafetyAccidents 《( 生產安全事故報告和調查處
理條例》), the Notice on Regulating the Inspection for Acceptance upon Completion of Safety
Facilities in Metal and Non-metal Mine Construction Projects 《( 關於規範金屬非金屬礦山建設項目
安全設施竣工驗收工作的通知》), the authorities in charge of mining enterprises under the people’s
governments at or above the county level shall exercise the following functions and responsibilities
with respect to the control of safety work in mines: (i) to inspect the implementation of laws and
regulations on safety in mines by mining enterprises; (ii) to examine and approve designs of safety
facilities in mine construction projects; (iii) to supervise the inspection for acceptance upon
completion of safety facilities in mine construction projects; (iv) to manage the training of managers
of mines and personnel in charge of safety work in mining enterprises; (v) to investigate and handle
work safety accidents at mines; and (vi) other controlling functions and responsibilities provided for
in laws and administrative rules and regulations. Upon occurrence of accidents, mining enterprises
shall immediately take measures to rescue their workers and report any casualty to the relevant
authority. In the event of a general mine accident, the mining enterprise shall be responsible for
investigating and handling the case. In the event of a fatal accident, the government, the relevant
authority, the labour union and the mining enterprise shall conduct investigation and handle the case
together. In addition, mining enterprise shall pay compensation to any staff who was injured or died
in the accident in accordance with the national requirements. Such mining enterprise may only resume
production after the relevant danger at the scene has been eliminated.
Pursuant to the Measures on the Implementation of Work Safety Permit for Non-Coal Mining
Enterprises 《( 非煤礦礦山企業安全生產許可證實施辦法》) (which came into effect on 17 May 2004
and revised on 8 June 2009 and 26 May 2015, respectively), non-coal mining enterprises must obtain
the production safety permit and are prohibited from engaging in any production activities without
obtaining the permit.
REGULATIONS ON TAXATION
Enterprise Income Tax
The Enterprise Income Tax Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國企業所得稅法》) promulgated by
the NPC on 16 March 2007, became effective on 1 January 2008 and amended on 24 February 2017
and 29 December 2018, respectively, as well as the Implementation Rules of the Enterprise Income
Tax Law 《( 中華人民共和國企業所得稅法實施條例》) promulgated by the State Council on 6
− 122 −

=== PAGE 133 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
December 2007, became effective on 1 January 2008 and amended on 23 April 2019 and 6 December
2024, are the principal law and regulation governing enterprise income tax in the PRC. According to
the Enterprise Income Tax Law and the Implementation Rules of the Enterprise Income Tax Law,
enterprises are classified into resident enterprises and non-resident enterprises. Resident enterprises
refer to enterprises that are legally established in the PRC, or are established under foreign laws but
whose actual management bodies are located in the PRC. And non-resident enterprises refer to
enterprises that are legally established under foreign laws and have set up institutions or sites in the
PRC but with no actual management body in the PRC, or enterprises that have not set up institutions
or sites in the PRC but have derived incomes from the PRC.Auniform income tax rate of 25% applies
to all resident enterprises and non-resident enterprises that have set up institutions or sites in the PRC
to the extent that such incomes are derived from their set-up institutions or sites in the PRC, or such
income are obtained outside the PRC but have an actual connection with the set-up institutions or
sites. For industries and projects which receive key support and encouragement for development from
the State, preferential treatment on enterprise income tax will be available.
According to the Announcement on Continuation of Enterprise Income Tax Policies for the
Large-scale Development in the Western Region 《( 關於延續西部大開發企業所得稅政策的公告》)
promulgated by the MOF, the SAT and the NDRC on 23April 2020, during the period from 1 January
2021 to 31 December 2030, Enterprise Income Tax shall be levied at a reduced tax rate of 15% on
enterprises established in the western region in encouraged industries. In accordance with the
Temporary Measures for the Implementation of Enterprise Income Tax Policies in the Xizang 《( 西藏
自治區企業所得稅政策實施辦法(暫行)》) promulgated by the People’s Government of Xizang on 29
April 2022, enterprises established in the western region in encouraged industries in the Xizang
Autonomous Region shall continue to implement the Enterprise Income Tax rate of 15% in the policy
of the Large-scale Development in the Western Region.
Value Added Tax
According to the Temporary Regulations on Value Added Tax of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國增
值稅暫行條例》) (“VAT Regulations”), which was promulgated by the State Council on 13 December
1993, came into effect on 1 January 1994, and was amended on 10 November 2008, on 6 February
2016 and 19 November 2017, respectively, and the Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the VAT
Regulations 《( 中華人民共和國增值稅暫行條例實施細則》), which was promulgated by the MOF and
came into effect on 25 December 1993 and was amended on 15 December 2008 and 28 October 2011,
respectively, all taxpayers selling goods, providing processing, repairing or replacement services or
importing goods within the PRC shall pay value added tax. Other than those as specified in the VAT
Regulations, the tax rate of 17% shall be levied on taxpayers selling or importing various goods, and
providing processing, repairing or replacement service. According to the Notice of the MOF and the
SAT on Adjusting Value added Tax Rates 《( 財政部、國家稅務總局關於調整增值稅稅率的通知》)
which was issued on 4 April 2018 and became effective on 1 May 2018, the deduction rates of 17%
and 11% applicable to the taxpayers who have value added tax taxable sales activities or imported
goods are adjusted to 16% and 10%, respectively. According to the Notice on Relevant Policies for
Deepening Value Added Tax Reform 《( 關於深化增值稅改革有關政策的公告》) which was issued on
20 March 2019 by the MOF, the SATand the GeneralAdministration of Customs and became effective
on 1 April 2019, the value added tax rate was reduced to 13% and 9%, respectively.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
On 25 December 2024, the Value-added Tax Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國增值稅法》) was
promulgated by the SCNPC, which will come into effect from 1 January 2026.
Urban Maintenance and Construction Tax
In accordance with the Urban Maintenance and Construction Tax Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民
共和國城市維護建設稅法》) which was promulgated by the SCNPC on 11August 2020 and came into
effect on 1 September 2021, entities and individuals which are subject to value added tax and
consumption tax, shall pay urban maintenance and construction tax. The tax rate is 7% for a taxpayer
who is domiciled in a downtown area, and 5% for a taxpayer who is domiciled in a county or town,
and 1% for a taxpayer who is domiciled outside a downtown area, county or town.
REGULATIONS ON EMPLOYMENT AND SOCIAL SECURITIES
Employment
Pursuant to the Labor Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國勞動法》) which was promulgated by
the SCNPC on 5 July 1994 and subsequently amended on 27August 2009 and 29 December 2018, the
Labor Contract Law of the PRC《(中華人民共和國勞動合同法》) which was promulgated by the
SCNPC on 29 June 2007 and subsequently amended on 28 December 2012 and the Implementing
Regulations of the Labor Contract Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國勞動合同法實施條例》) which
was promulgated by the State Council on 18 September 2008, labour contracts in written form shall
be needed to establish labour relationships between employers and employees. Wages cannot be lower
than the local standards of minimum wages. The employer must establish the system of occupational
safety and sanitation, strictly implement the rules and standards of the State, provide education
regarding occupational safety and sanitation among employees, provide employees with labour safety
and sanitation conditions and necessary articles of labour protection conforming to the provisions of
the State, and provide regular health examination for employees engaged in work involving
occupational hazards.
Social Insurance and Housing Provident Funds
Under applicable PRC laws related to the social insurance, including the Social Insurance Law
of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國社會保險法》) which was promulgated by the SCNPC on 28 October
2010 and amended on 29 December 2018, the Interim Regulations on Levying Social Insurance
Premiums 《( 社會保險費徵繳暫行條例》) which was promulgated by the State Council on 22 January
1999 and amended on 24 March 2019, and the Administrative Regulations on the Housing Provident
Fund 《( 住房公積金管理條例》) which was promulgated by the State Council on 3 April 1999,
amended on 24 March 2002 and 24 March 2019, respectively, employers are required to contribute,
on behalf of their employees, to a number of social security funds, including funds for basic pension
insurance, unemployment insurance, basic medical insurance, occupational injury insurance,
maternity insurance and to housing provident funds. These payments are made to local administrative
authorities and any employer who fails to contribute may be ordered to make good the deficit within
a stipulated time limit and fined.
− 124 −

=== PAGE 135 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
On July 31, 2025, the PRC Supreme People’s Court promulgated the Supreme People’s Court’s
Interpretation (II) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Labor Dispute Cases 《( 最
高人民法院關於審理勞動爭議案件適用法律問題的解釋(二)》), (the “New Judicial Interpretation),
which took effect on September 1, 2025. Article 19(1) thereof stipulates that if an employer and an
employee agree or the employee undertakes that social insurance contributions need not be paid, the
court shall deem such agreement or undertaking invalid. Furthermore, where an employer fails to pay
social insurance contributions in accordance with the law, and the employee seeks to terminate the
labor contract and claims economic compensation from the employer pursuant to Article 38(3) of the
PRC Labor Contract Law, the court shall support such claims in accordance with the law, which
clarifies that employees are entitled to request termination of their labor contracts and receive
corresponding economic compensation under the PRC Labor Contract Law if the employer fails to
make social insurance contributions in accordance with the law.
Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases
According to the Law of the PRC on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases 《( 中
華人民共和國職業病防治法》), which was promulgated by the SCNPC on 27 October 2001 and was
revised on 31 December 2011, 2 July 2016, 4 November 2017 and 29 December 2018, respectively,
a construction entity shall conduct the pre-assessment of occupational hazards at the feasibility study
stage if a construction project may cause any occupational hazards. The protective facilities against
occupational diseases of the construction project shall be designed, constructed, and put to use in
production and other operations at the same time as the main body of the project. And before the
acceptance check of a construction project, the construction entity shall evaluate the effects of
occupational hazard control.
REGULATIONS ON INTELLECTUAL PROPERTIES
Patents
Pursuant to the Patent Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國專利法》), promulgated by the SCNPC
on 12 March 1984 and latest amended on 17 October 2020 and became effective as from 1 June 2021,
the Implementation Rules of the Patent Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國專利法實施細則》) which
was promulgated by the State Council on 15 June 2001 and latest amended on 11 December 2023 and
became effective as from 20 January 2024, and the Public Announcement on Measures on Filing of
Patent Licensing Contracts 《( 專利實施許可合同備案辦法》) which was promulgated by the State
Intellectual Property Office on 27 June 2011 and became effective on 1 August 2011, there are three
types of patent in the PRC: invention patent, utility model patent and design patent. The current
protection period is 20 years for invention patent, 10 years for utility model patent and 15 years for
design patent, commencing from their respective application dates. Any individual or entity that
utilises a patent or conducts any other activity in infringement of a patent without prior authorisation
of the patentee shall pay compensation to the patentee and is subject to a fine imposed by relevant
administrative authorities and, if constituting a crime, shall be held criminally liable in accordance
with the law. Any organisation or individual proposing to implement the patent of others shall enter
into a licensing contract with the patentee for implementation and pay royalties to the patentee. The
parties concerned shall complete filing formalities within three months from the effective date of a
patent licensing contract. And the State Intellectual Property Office shall be responsible for filing of
patent licensing contracts nationwide.

=== PAGE 136 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Domain names
In accordance with the Administrative Measures for Internet Domain Names 《( 互聯網域名管理
辦法》), which was issued by the MIIT on 24 August 2017 and effective as at 1 November 2017, the
Implementing Rules for the Registration of National Top-level Domain Names 《( 國家頂級域名註冊
實施細則》) and Procedural Rules for Resolution of Disputes over National Top-level Domain Names
(《國家頂級域名爭議解決程序規則》) which were promulgated by China Internet Network
Information Centre on June 18, 2019 and came into effect on the same date, the MIIT is the main
regulatory body responsible for the administration of the PRC internet domain names. Domain name
registrations are handled through domain name service agencies established under the relevant
regulations. The domain name services follow a “apply first, register first” principle. Applicants for
registration of domain names shall provide their true, accurate and complete information of such
domain names to and enter into registration agreements with domain name registration service
institutions. The applicants shall become the holders of such domain names upon successful
registration. The domain name disputes shall be accepted and solved by a domain name dispute
resolution body as recognised by the China Internet Network Information Centre.
REGULATIONS ON OVERSEAS SECURITIES OFFERING AND LISTING BY DOMESTIC
COMPANIES
On 17 February 2023, the CSRC promulgated the Trial Administrative Measures of Overseas
Securities Offering and Listing by Domestic Companies 《( 境內企業境外發行證券和上市管理試行辦
法》) (“Overseas Listing Trial Measures”) and relevant supporting guidelines, which came into
effect on 31 March 2023.The Overseas ListingTrial Measures comprehensively improves and reforms
the existing regulatory regime for overseas offering and listing of PRC domestic companies’securities
and regulates both direct and indirect overseas offering and listing of PRC domestic companies’
securities. Any domestic company that is deemed to conduct overseas offering and listing activities
shall file with the CSRC in accordance with the Overseas Listing Trial Measures.
The Overseas ListingTrial Measures provide that the overseas securities offering and listing will
be considered a direct overseas offering by a PRC domestic company if the issuer is a company
limited by shares registered and established in mainland China. Pursuant to the Overseas Listing Trial
Measures, an issuer shall file with the CSRC within three business days after its application for initial
public offering is submitted to competent overseas securities regulators. Failure to complete the filing
under the Overseas Listing Trial Measures may subject a PRC domestic enterprise to rectification
ordered by the CSRC, warning, and fine of RMB1 million to RMB10 million.
A domestic enterprise that intends to be listed or is listed overseas may raise funds and pay
dividends in foreign currencies or RMB. The use and investment of proceeds from overseas issuance
by a domestic enterprise shall comply with the laws, administrative regulations and relevant national
rules. The foreign exchange and cross-border flow of capitals relating to the overseas issuance and
listing of a domestic enterprise shall comply with the national regulations on cross-border investment
and financing, foreign exchange management, and cross-border RMB management.
− 126 −

=== PAGE 137 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
The Overseas Listing Administrative Measures provide that an overseas offering and listing is
explicitly prohibited under any of the following circumstances: (1) if the offering and listing is
specifically prohibited by laws, administrative regulations and relevant national provisions; (2) if the
overseas offering and listing constitutes endangers to national security as reviewed and determined by
competent authorities under the State Council in accordance with law; (3) if, in the past three years,
the domestic enterprise or its controlling shareholders or actual controllers have committed
corruption, bribery, embezzlement, misappropriation of property, or other criminal offenses disruptive
to the order of the socialist market economy; (4) if the domestic enterprise is under investigation
according to law for suspected crimes or major violations of laws and regulations, but no clear
conclusions have been reached; or (5) if there are material ownership disputes over the equity held
by the controlling shareholder or by other shareholders that are controlled by the controlling
shareholder and/or actual controller.

HISTORY AND CORPORATE STRUCTURE
OVERVIEW
We are a mining company focusing our business on zinc, lead and copper exploration, mining,
production and sales of concentrates based in Xizang, China. Our business is located in Rongdoi
Township, Jiali County, Nagqu, Xizang. We hold exploration rights over an area of approximately
58.5 sq.km and mining rights over 4.5 sq.km, respectively. Since our inception, we have been
leveraging Xizang’s unique geological conditions and rich mineral resources, backed by favourable
government initiatives in support of the region’s mining industries. According to SMM, we ranked
fifth in terms of the annual production volume of zinc concentrates, fourth in terms of the annual
production volume of lead concentrates, and fifth in terms of the annual production volume of copper
concentrates, in Xizang in 2024.
The history of our Company can be traced back to 2013 when our Company was established in
Xizang, the PRC by Ms. Fan, our founder. From 2013 to 2024, our Company went through a series
of capital increase and brought in new Shareholders. See “— Our Corporate Development” in this
section for further details. On 18 December 2020, our Company was converted into a joint stock
limited company and we changed our Company’s name from Xizang Zhihui Industrial Co., Ltd. (西
藏智匯實業有限公司) to Xizang Zhihui Mining Co., Ltd.* (西藏智匯礦業股份有限公司).

reputable stock exchange, to be a more appropriate listing venue, our Company voluntarily decided
not to continue the A Share Listing Attempt in 2024 and to pursue a listing in Hong Kong. We were
given to understand that the duration of our A Share Listing Attempt’s guidance filing was not
abnormally prolonged compared to the standard A-share guidance filing practices, based on the
observations from several independent market practitioners with experience inA-share listings.As at
the Latest Practicable Date, our Company did not submit any formal listing application in relation to

accessing wider capital fund pool and promoting our Group to global investors, which in turn provides
further capital to bolster our business development and international expansion efforts, and to
strengthen our Group’s working capital. For details of our application of proceeds from the Listing,

Immediately upon completion of the Global Offering, our Company will have a total number of
487,805,659 Shares, comprising 365,853,659 Domestic Shares and 121,952,000 H Shares.
365,853,659 Domestic Shares, including 365,853,659 Domestic Shares held by our Controlling

will be counted towards the public float.
With respect to the indicative Offer Price range of HK$4.10, HK$4.30 and HK$4.51 per Offer
Share (being the low-end, mid-point and the high-end of the Offer Price, respectively), the expected
market capitalization of the Company’s H Shares at the time of Listing will be approximately HK$2.0
billion, HK$2.1 billion and HK$2.2 billion, respectively. Under Rule 19A.13A(1) of the Listing
Rules, in the event the expected market value of the Company’s H Shares upon Listing does not
exceed HK$6 billion, at least 25% of the total issued H Shares must be held by the public upon
Listing, and the Company’s expected public float of 25% will satisfy the minimum public float
requirement under Rule 19A.13A(1) of the Listing Rules.

FREE FLOAT
Rule 19A.13C of the Listing Rules provides that, where a new applicant is a PRC issuer with no
other listed shares at the time of Listing, this will normally mean that the portion of H shares for
which listing is sought that are held by the public and not subject to any disposal restrictions (whether
under contract, the Listing Rules, applicable laws or otherwise), at the time of listing, must:(a)
represent at least 10% of the total number of issued shares in the class to which H shares belong at
the time of listing (excluding treasury shares), with an expected market value at the time of listing
of not less than HK$50,000,000; or (b) have an expected market value at the time of listing of not less
than HK$600,000,000. Our Company will satisfy the free float requirement under Rule 19A.13C of
the Listing Rules.

BUSINESS
OVERVIEW
We are a mining company focusing our business on zinc, lead and copper exploration, mining,
production and sales of concentrates based in Xizang, China. According to SMM, in terms of the
average annual production volume in Xizang in 2024, we ranked fifth for zinc concentrates, fourth for
lead concentrates and fifth for copper concentrates.
Our business is located in Rongdoi Township, Jiali County, Nagqu, Xizang. Our Mengya’a Mine
comprises an open-pit mine which is in its commercial operation stage, and an underground mine,
which has commenced commercial operation since the second quarter of 2025. Our mining operation
is located within the nationally designated Jinda Integrated Exploration Area at an altitude between
5,000.0 m asl and 5,300.0 m asl where rich mineral resources have been found. We hold exploration
rights over an area of approximately 58.5 sq.km and mining rights over an area of approximately 4.5
sq.km, respectively. With our ESG commitment, our Mengya’a Mine has been selected in the List of
National Green Mine 《( 綠色礦山名錄》) by the Ministry of Natural Resources of the PRC (中華人民
共和國自然資源部). Safety is our first priority. We were awarded the “2024 Annual Regional Safety
Production Advanced Enterprise (2024年度全區安全生產先進企業)” by Xizang Autonomous Region
Department of Emergency Management (西藏自治區應急管理廳). As a mining company in Xizang,
we believe we need to consistently adopt a localised business approach, taking into account the unique
geological conditions and Xizang’s specific policies to ensure our business can adapt to the local
conditions and lead to ongoing business sustainability and success. As at 31 July 2025, our open-pit
mine contained total Ore Reserves of 1,438.0 kt at average grades of 4.90% Zn, 0.69% Pb, 0.10% Cu
and 10.09 g/t Ag; and our underground mine contained total Ore Reserves of 10,623.0 kt at average
grades of 4.14% Zn, 2.99% Pb, 0.21% Cu and 35.00 g/t Ag. Our Mengya’a Mine can, in aggregate,
supply 400.0 kt of ores annually for concentrate production at our processing plant.
We have a business operation chain that encompasses exploration, mining, production, and sales
of concentrates. Our main products include zinc concentrates, lead concentrates and copper
concentrates. During the Track Record Period, our revenue was generated from sales of these
concentrates to our customers in China. Our customers included nonferrous metal traders who
generally conducted onward sales of concentrates to end users of concentrates; and refineries who
further processed our concentrates depending on their customers’ needs. We possess solid experience
of producing lead, zinc and copper concentrates; and we have received multiple awards and accolades.
Notably, we were awarded the “China Nonferrous Metals Industry Science and Technology Award”
(中國有色金屬工業科學技術獎) by the China Nonferrous Metals IndustryAssociation (中國有色金屬
工業協會) and the Nonferrous Metals Society of China (中國有色金屬學會) in 2019. We are
committed to unlocking the potential of Xizang’s mining industry, by leveraging Xizang’s unique
geological conditions and rich mineral resources. We also aim to implement advanced technologies
and innovative practices throughout our business operations.

The following flowchart illustrates our business operation chain.
Business Operation Chain
Exploration Mining Production Sales of Concentrates
(identifying and assessing (extracting minerals) (consisting of both ore (sales of concentrates to
mineral deposits) processing and concentrate nonferrous metal traders
production processes) and refineries)
• Exploration: Exploration is the initial phase which involves identifying and assessing
mineral deposits through geological surveys, sampling and drilling. Exploration of mining
resources in Xizang is inherently challenging due to the region’s rugged terrain, high
altitudes and harsh weather conditions, which can hinder accessibility and operational
efficiency. These factors require specialised techniques and professional planning to
effectively assess and develop the mineral potential in this unique environment. Some of
our exploration team members possess more than a decade of exploration experience in
Xizang, thereby deeply understanding Xizang’s resources. We benefit from technical
support and engage qualified external teams for some tasks. In respect of geophysical
exploration, our exploration team has collaborated with the Second Brigade of the Xizang
Autonomous Region Geological and Mineral Exploration and Development Bureau (西藏
自治區地質礦產勘查開發局地質二隊) and Xizang Chuandi Geology Survey Engineering
Company Limited (西藏川地地質勘查工程有限公司). In respect of testing and analysis,
our exploration team has collaborated with Lhasa Jinzangyan MineralAnalysis and Testing
Company Limited (拉薩金藏岩礦分析測試有限公司). Through these collaborations, we
have a solid grasp of the characteristics and conditions of Xizang’s terrain and mining
areas, including accessibility, climate, physiography and the technical challenges they may
present, enabling us to develop solutions for more efficient exploration efforts.

BUSINESS
Our exploration team utilises analytical methods to evaluate the potential of various sites
in Xizang, ensuring that we focus on areas with the highest likelihood of yielding valuable
ores (i.e., ores that at least meet the cut-off grade for concentrate production purpose). We
have also conducted research in collaboration with China University of Geosciences
(中國地質大學) in the field of exploration. Through this collaboration, we successfully
identified a new method for exploring potential mineral resources based on the variation
of indicator elements in greenstone (基於綠泥石指示元素變化判別找礦類型的新辦法),
which is a core invention patent among our intellectual property portfolio. Meanwhile, we
place great emphasis on the innovation of exploration equipment to enhance our
exploration efficiency with new technologies. To this end, we strengthen R&D efforts in
developing new equipment and devices used in our ore exploration activities.As at 31 July
2025, we possessed two utility model accreditations for our ore exploration equipment, and
our exploration team consisted of five geologists, among which two held Senior Engineer
Qualification Certificates (高級工程師資格證書) in the PRC. During the Track Record
Period, while we are responsible for planning, formulating implementation plans and
overseeing quality control for exploration and mining activities, all exploration and mining
operations are entirely outsourced to subcontractors. See “— Mining — Exploration and
Mining Subcontracting Arrangement” in this section for details.
• Mining: Once a viable deposit is confirmed, we may proceed to the mining phase. This
involves extracting minerals by applying specific techniques based on our exploration
mining studies and results. We have been using open-pit mining technique for our open-pit
operations, and we have commenced the commercial operation of the underground mine
since the second quarter of 2025. Our mining operations prioritise safety, efficiency and
minimal environmental impact.
Based on exploration and technical studies results, appropriate mining methods for
open-pit or underground mining are determined, and the necessary infrastructure, including
roads, power supply and water resource management systems, is planned. Once all required
licences and permits are obtained, we enter into the mining preparation phase, which
generally involves site clearing and the establishment of facilities such as mine entrances,
crushing stations and concentrators. During the actual mining process, if the open-pit
mining method is applied, the overburden must first be removed, and blasting techniques
are applied to break large ore blocks for transport. In the case of underground mining, a
network of access tunnels is created, along with measures to ensure tunnel stability. Upon
the conclusion of mining process, ores will be transported to our processing plant.
Meanwhile, we will record the quantity of the ores that have been extracted, ensuring
compliance with the annual mining limit volume stipulated in our mining licence.
During the Track Record Period, we engaged three subcontractors in respect of our mining
works. As these subcontractors were also instructed to undertake exploration works, we
gave them clear guidelines prior to the commencement of any exploration and mining
works, ensuring exploration and mining works can be conducted in accordance with our
technical studies. Ores are transported to our processing plant. Currently, we have one
processing plant, which is located in a valley 10.0 km north of our mining site. During the
Track Record Period, we engaged two transportation service providers which were
responsible for transporting ores to our processing plant.
− 142 −

=== PAGE 153 ===
BUSINESS
We also purchased high-grade ores from independent third party ore suppliers in 2024 and
2025. See “— Mining — Management Discussion on Ore Procurement” in this section for
details.
• Production: Production consists of two steps including ore processing and concentrate
production. Ores are processed at our processing plant, namely, Mengya’a Beneficiation
Plant, to produce concentrates. The production of our zinc, lead and copper concentrates
involves several key stages, starting with crushing and grinding to reduce the ore size and
liberate valuable ore minerals. Next, concentration methods, primarily representing
flotation, are employed to separate valuable ore minerals from gauge minerals, by using
chemicals to create bubbles that allow targeted minerals to float to the surface. The
concentrated ores are subsequently filtered and dried to remove moisture to achieve the
desired purity in accordance with the requisite industry standards and our customers’
requests. Throughout this process, proper management and disposal of waste materials and
tailings are essential to minimise environmental impacts.
The improvement of grinding fineness is a key aspect of our production process, which
requires blending due to the high impurity content in ores. Additionally, high-grade ores
and mineralised waste may also be blended economically for us to produce feed ores that
meet the specifications for concentrate production purpose. By replacing and upgrading the
grinding cyclone classifier, we have increased the original grinding fineness from 65.0 to
70.0% passing 74.0 µm to 70.0 to 75.0% passing 74.0 µm. Additionally, we have
implemented a fully enclosed water recycling system without discharge, which has earned
us “China Nonferrous Metals Industry Science and TechnologyAward” (中國有色金屬工業
科學技術獎) in December 2019. We also introduced new beneficiation equipment in 2024,
including flotation columns with an aim to improve the quantity and quality of our
concentrates.
• Sales of concentrates: Our three main mineral products represent zinc concentrates, lead
concentrates and copper concentrates, each of which play a significant role in various
industries. All of our revenue was generated from sale of concentrates. Generally speaking,
lead concentrates are crucial for the production of batteries, radiation shielding and a
variety of alloys, making them indispensable in the automotive and electronics sectors.
Zinc concentrates are primarily used for galvanising steel to prevent corrosion, as well as
in the manufacturing of brass and other alloys. In parallel, copper concentrates can be used
in electrical applications attributable to their excellent conductivity and are widely used in
wiring, plumbing and electronic devices. During the Track Record Period, our customers
consisted of (i) nonferrous metal traders who generally conducted onward sales to end
users of concentrates; and (ii) refineries which further processed our concentrates based on
the needs of their customers.

We believe that the following strengths provide the foundation of our position as one of the

We enjoy a distinct advantage in Xizang for our sufficient and high-calibre mineral resources
given the region’s geographical characteristics
We enjoy a distinct advantage in Xizang, attributable to our abundant and high-quality mineral
resources, which are enhanced by the region’s favourable geographical characteristics. Our mining
operations are centred around rich polymetallic resources, representing zinc, lead and copper, which
serve as our main processing materials. As at 31 July 2025, our open-pit mine contained total Ore
Reserves of 1,438.0 kt at average grades of 4.90% Zn, 0.69% Pb, 0.10% Cu and 10.09 g/tAg; and our
underground mine contained total Ore Reserves of 10,623.0 kt at average grades of 4.14% Zn, 2.99%
Pb, 0.21% Cu and 35.00 g/t Ag. This reliability plays a crucial role in supporting our long-term
concentrate production activities and sales strategies, ensures our sustainable growth and fosters our
position us as an active and leading market player in Xizang.
The relatively complex geological structure of the Xizang Plateau creates ideal conditions for
the formation of a wide array of both metallic and non-metallic mineral resources. This rich
geological diversity is not a mere natural asset; it also serves as the essential foundation for our
business sustainability and growth. The unique geological formations and processes in the region
contribute to the concentration of valuable minerals, allowing us to tap into substantial reserves that
are critical for our business operations. The said geological richness significantly reduces the costs
and risks associated with exploring and developing new mining sites. With a well-defined
understanding of Xizang’s geology, we are able to strategically target exploration efforts, leading to
more efficient resource identification and extraction. This targeted approach minimises uncertainties
and enhances the overall productivity of our mining operations. Additionally, the favourable
geological conditions indicate that we can expect higher-quality mineral deposits, which further
streamline our concentrate production. The combination of reduced exploration risks and access to
high-grade ores not only improves our mining operational efficiency but also strengthens our
competitive position in the mining market, known for the provision of our high-calibre concentrates.
As we continue to leverage the geological advantage of Xizang, we are well-equipped to sustain our
growth and meet the increasing demands for our products, being zinc, lead and copper concentrates.
This is testified by our effort and success in developing our underground mine in Xizang, which has
commenced its commercial operation since the second quarter of 2025, and can supply, in aggregate,
400.0 kt of ores annually to our processing plant.
