OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY
We are subject to various PRC laws and regulations with respect to labour, safety and
work-related incidents. See “Regulatory Overview” in this prospectus for the key PRC laws and
regulations applicable to our business operations.
We are committed to maintaining a safe working environment and promoting the awareness of
occupational health and safety. We are also responsible for implementing safety measures to ensure
a safe and healthy workplace, as some of our business activities involve usage of dangerous products,
explosives, for example, in connection with extracting ores during the mining phase of our business
operation chain. Our management also ensures that necessary information, instruction and supervision
are provided so that all employees are safe from injury and health risks. We organise safety
orientations for new employees to keep them informed and train them in relation to offering to safety
regulations and emergency procedures. The emergency procedures such as fire or explosion
emergency plans have been fully established, and we regularly arrange rescue, fire and evacuation
drills in order to prevent casualties in case of accidents.
− 236 −

=== PAGE 247 ===
BUSINESS
Our Directors have confirmed that during the Track Record Period and up to the Latest
Practicable Date, we complied with all relevant safety laws and regulations in all material respects.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, the relevant PRC authorities
had not imposed any sanction, penalty, fines or punishment on us for any non-compliance with any
health and safety laws or regulations in the PRC. Due to the nature of our business, we may
occasionally encounter some workplace injuries. However, as our employees are all covered by
comprehensive workers’ compensation insurance, these occasional injuries have never had a
significant adverse impact on our business operations and financial performance historically and
during the Track Record Period.
On 23 April 2023, a workforce accident occurred at the entrance of our Phase 2 Tailings Pond
within the mining site area of our subsidiary, Huaxia Mining. An employee of our contractor, who was
responsible for constructing the Phase 2 Tailings Pond was inspecting a vehicle when the cylinder
suddenly depressurised, causing the bucket to drop and crush the said employee’s back. The said
employee died despite all rescue efforts. According to the accident report, the direct cause of the
casualty was attributable to the failure to use secondary support while inspecting the vehicle, which
constituted a contravention of applicable safety regulations.
The Emergency Management Bureau of Jiali County（嘉黎縣應急管理局）and the Jiali County
People’s Government（嘉黎縣人民政府）issued a written confirmation, confirming that:
(i) the occurrence of the incident was in the mining site area of Huaxia Mining and the
incident was adjudged as a general safety incident (一般性安全生產事故);
(ii) Huaxia Mining complied with its reporting obligations as stipulated by the Regulations on
Reporting and Investigation of Production SafetyAccidents 《( 生產安全事故報告和調查處
理條例》);
(iii) according to the investigation findings of the incident, Huaxia Mining was not held liable
for this incident and had not been involved in any safety production accidents since 1
January 2022; and
(iv) Huaxia Mining has not been subject to administrative penalties, such as licence suspension,
fines, or death compensation.
Furthermore, according to the investigation findings of the incident and the Explanation of the
Situation Regarding the Safety Incident at Xizang Huaxia 《( 關於西藏華夏礦業安全事故的情況說
明》) issued by the Economic and Information Bureau of Nagqu City (那曲市經濟和信息化局), we
were not found to be liable for the incident.
− 237 −

=== PAGE 248 ===
BUSINESS
Our PRC LegalAdvisers have confirmed that the accident which occurred on 23April 2023 was
categorised as a “general production safety accident” (一般生產安全事故). A general accident does
not trigger the restrictive measures set out in the Notice of the State Council on Further Strengthening
Enterprise Safety Production Work 《( 國務院關於進一步加強企業安全生產工作的通知》). During the
Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, no other accident experienced by the
Group fell within any of those prescribed thresholds. Consequently, the restrictive measures,
including limitations on new project approvals, land use rights, securities financing and bank lending,
are inapplicable to the Group. As no such restrictions have been or are expected to be imposed, the
accident has had no material adverse impact on the Group’s operations or financial performance.
The Emergency Management Bureau of Jiali County and the Jiali County People’s Government
are the competent authorities to classify and confirm a general production safety accident under
Article 19 of the Regulation on the Reporting, Investigation and Handling of Production Safety
Accidents 《( 生產安全事故報告和調查處理條例》) and Article 6 of the Measures on Fines for
Production Safety Accidents 《( 生產安全事故罰款處罰規定》), which allocate the investigation,
approval and penalty powers for general accidents to the county level. Although the Economic and
Information Bureau of Nagqu City is not a safety regulator, it issued a factual statement on 9 July
2024 in its capacity as the municipal bureau subordinate to the Autonomous Region’s Department of
Economy and Information Technology, which is the authority supervising the Group’s qualification as
an “Autonomous Region Green Supply Chain Management Enterprise”. That statement therefore has
reference value in affirming that the accident does not affect the Group’s green-supply-chain status.
The confirmations given by the Jiali County Emergency Management Bureau and the Jiali County
People’s Government are not administrative penalty decisions, but descriptive confirmations of
objective facts within their jurisdiction.
Under both the PRC Work Safety Law 《( 中華人民共和國安全生產法》) and the Interim
Measures on Safety Management of Outsourced Works in Non-coal Mines 《( 非煤礦山外包工程安全
管理暫行辦法》), liability for an accident is ultimately determined by the official accident
investigation report and its governmental approval. In the present case, Jiali County People’s
Government, the authority responsible for approving investigations into general work safety
accidents, confirmed in its 16 January 2025 letter that it had fulfilled all of its statutory duties and
that no administrative penalties were imposed on Huaxia Mining in connection with the accident.
Save for the accident on 23April 2023, no other production safety accidents occurred within the
Group during the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date.
Based on the above, our Directors have confirmed that the incident did not have any material
impact on our business operation and financial performance, nor there is any indication that there is
any deficiency of our safety internal control measure. Save for the said incident, there was no other
safety incident in the ordinary course of our mining operations during the Track Record Period and
up to the Latest Practicable Date.

=== PAGE 249 ===
BUSINESS
We have implemented the following measures to strength contractor and subcontractor
management to prevent the occurrence of similar accidents:
• Careful vetting and selection of contractors and subcontractors: Adopt enhanced
evaluation procedures for the vetting and selection of contractors and subcontractors,
which include, but are not limited to, a comprehensive review of their credentials, safety
measures and historical safety performance records. This process involves carefully
assessing their professional licences and industry qualifications, the effectiveness of
contractors’ and subcontractors’ safety protocols, examining past incidents or violations,
and evaluating their overall commitment to maintaining a safe working environment.
Contractors and subcontractors with a documented history of poor safety performance or
non-compliance with safety standards, or without the requisite credentials, will be screened
out and excluded from consideration.
• Prohibition of unauthorised subcontracting:To maintain control over project quality and
safety standards, contractors are expressly prohibited from engaging any subcontractors
without first obtaining our prior written consent. This measure allows us to carefully
review and approve all subcontracting arrangements, ensuring that every party involved in
the project aligns with our established safety protocols and performance expectations. We
can prevent unauthorised subcontracting that may compromise safety or quality, and ensure
consistent adherence to regulatory requirements and internal standards.
Further, we have taken the following enhanced internal control measures to prevent the
occurrence of similar incidents:
• Comprehensive Training: Regularly provide all employees with comprehensive safety
training, covering emergency response, equipment operation standards, and personal
protective measures. New employees must undergo basic safety knowledge training upon
hiring and pass an assessment before starting work. Current employees should participate
in refresher training at least once a year to update and reinforce their safety awareness and
skills.
• Strict Inspection Protocols: Establish and enforce a rigorous safety inspection system to
ensure that all production equipment and work environments meet national safety
standards. Create a dedicated safety inspection team responsible for routine and special
inspections to promptly identify and eliminate potential hazards. For critical equipment,
develop detailed maintenance plans and strictly adhere to them, documenting each
inspection and maintenance activity for effective tracking and management.
• Detailed Emergency Plans: Develop comprehensive emergency response plans that cover
various potential emergencies, such as fires, explosions, and collapses. Organise regular
drills for all employees to enhance their ability to respond to unforeseen events. The
emergency plans should clearly outline the specific responsibilities of each department and
individual during an incident, ensuring swift and accurate information transfer and
efficient, orderly rescue operations. Additionally, regularly assess and refine the plans,
adjusting them based on real circumstances to ensure they remain practical and effective.

Non-registration of lease agreements
As at the Latest Practicable Date, we had not yet registered our six lease agreements with the
local housing administration authorities as required under the relevant PRC laws, primarily due to the
limited cooperation from the landlords in registering the relevant lease agreements, which was beyond
our control; and due to the landlords’lack of title certificates. As advised by our PRC LegalAdvisers,
lease agreements have to be registered with the relevant authorities within 30 days of signing
according to theAdministration Measures for Commodity House Leasing 《( 商品房屋租賃管理辦法》)
and if we fail to rectify within a prescribed period, we may be subject to a maximum administrative
penalty of RMB10,000.0 for each unregistered lease. As at the Latest Practicable Date, we had not
received any notice from any regulatory authority with respect to potential administrative penalties
or enforcement actions due to our failure to register the lease agreements as set out above. Our PRC
LegalAdvisers further advised that the non-registration of lease agreements would however not affect
the enforceability of these lease agreements. Accordingly, our Directors are of the view that our
non-registration would not have any material adverse impact on our business operations.

QUALITY CONTROL
As a mining company, quality control is crucial to our mining operations. We have established
a stringent quality control system to ensure the quality of our concentrates. We are required to comply
with the applicable PRC laws and regulations in respect of our production. Set out below is a key
summary of the quality standards of our concentrates by type that we need to comply with.
• our zinc concentrate quality standards (excluding purity and impurity content agreed upon
with customers) conform to the National Standard for Zinc Concentrate of the PRC 《( 中
華人民共和國鋅精礦國家標準》) (YS/T320-2014 for grade III),
• our lead concentrate quality standards (excluding purity and impurity content agreed upon
with customers) conform to the National Standard for Lead Concentrate of the PRC 《( 中
華人民共和國鉛精礦國家標準》) (YS/T319-2013 for grades II and III), and
• our copper concentrate quality standards (excluding purity and impurity content agreed
upon with customers) conform to the National Standard for Copper Concentrate of the PRC
(《中華人民共和國銅精礦國家標準》) (YS/T318-2007 for grades III and IV).
During the Track Record Period, we did not encounter any concentrate quality issue, nor did we
have any product liability issue in the ordinary course of dealings with our customers.
We provide quality and technical specifications to suppliers and generally require suppliers to
provide warranty for the supplies we procure. We inspect the physical conditions and the quantities
received of each delivery of raw materials, consumables, parts and replacement before accepting the
products into our inventory. In terms of procurement of services, we engage contractors and
subcontractors for certain parts of the our mining operations, such as extracting ores in the mining
phase of our business operation chain, transportation and construction works of our underground mine
and Phase 2 Tailings Pond. We require all these contractors and subcontractors to meet our
qualification requirements and conduct their operations in accordance with our internal standards,
industry standards and the relevant PRC laws and regulations. We supervise and regularly inspect
their works to ensure their works are undertaken in accordance with our quality standards. We conduct
quality inspections when they have completed the works before we accept their works.

BUSINESS
We have established a comprehensive internal control framework to maintain rigorous oversight
of contractors and subcontractors, ensuring ongoing compliance with all applicable occupational
health and safety, environmental protection and licensing requirements:
• Oversight by different departments: Our Safety and Environment Department holds
primary responsibility for monitoring and enforcing compliance with workplace safety
standards and all relevant contractual obligations. The department conducts thorough
onsite inspections on a regular basis with other departments including the Engineering
Department, during which designated officers carry out detailed assessments of contractors
and subcontractors’ adherence to applicable occupational health and safety regulations,
environmental protection requirements and other statutory obligations. Additionally, these
officers verify the validity of all necessary licences, certifications and permits required for
the safe and lawful execution of their operations. Furthermore, our GeneralAdministration
Department oversees the administration of employment injury insurance for all employees
involved in mining activities.
• Incident reporting and rectification procedures: In the event that any non-compliance,
misconduct or violation of applicable rules or contractual terms is identified, officers from
the relevant internal departments and externally-engaged supervising engineers will
document the issue by completing a hazard rectification notice 《( 隱患整改通知單》).
Whereupon, the relevant contractors or subcontractors are promptly notified and required
to take immediate corrective action to address the identified deficiencies. To ensure
effective resolution, the departments and supervising engineers conduct follow-up
inspections to ensure that the corrective measures have been properly implemented and that
the non-compliance, misconduct, or violation has been fully rectified.
• General Supervising Office: We have established a General Supervising Office (總監辦)
tasked with coordinating communication between the relevant internal departments and all
contractors and subcontractors engaged in mining operations. This office actively monitors
the safety conditions of workers on site, ensuring that health and safety policies are
effectively implemented and that any emerging risks are promptly addressed.
• Emergency preparedness and regulatory compliance: To prepare for potential safety
incidents, we have developed the Production Safety Accident Emergency Response Plan
(《生產安全事故應急預案》). This plan provides clear guidance on procedures to be
followed in the event of an accident to minimise harm and ensure swift response. We have
also obtained official acknowledgment of this plan from the relevant regulatory authority.

Litigation
As at the Latest Practicable Date, Huludao Jinshun Mining Development Company Limited (葫
蘆島金順礦業開發有限公司) (“Jinshun Mining”)) filed a lawsuit against our subsidiary, Huaxia
Mining, in the Intermediate People’s Court of Lhasa (西藏自治區拉薩市中級人民法院) (the
“Intermediate Court”), seeking RMB10.8 million damages for service fees and affiliated claims
pursuant to a relevant service and claiming that Huaxia Mining failed to discharge its obligation to
settle outstanding payments owed to it. On 28 March 2025, the said court ruled that Jinshun Mining
should have sought arbitration as its first resort, thereby dismissing the lawsuit. In response to the
dismissal and on 3April 2025, Jinshun Mining made an appeal. On 26 May 2025, the Higher People’s
Court of TibetAutonomous Region (西藏自治區高級人民法院) (the “Higher Court”) issued a ruling,
holding that the arbitration clause in the said service agreement at issue was no longer valid, and that
the Intermediate Court should not have dismissed the lawsuit. The Higher Court therefore revoked the
Intermediate Court’s ruling and ordered the Intermediate Court to hear the case. On 13 June 2025, the
Intermediate Court served Huaxia Mining with a notice of response to the lawsuit. The case was heard
on 10 November 2025. As of the Latest Practicable Date, the case remains under trial.
Based on the public search records and as confirmed by our Directors, the legal representative
of Jinshun Mining had been repeatedly pursuing claims related to the said service agreement since
2007, all of which had been dismissed. A previous case ruling by the Higher Court in 2023, the court
held that the evidence submitted by the legal representative of Jinshun Mining could not prove that
there remained any clear creditor-debtor relationship between Jinshun Mining and Huaxia Mining.
The court found that such lawsuit lacked a factual basis and did not meet the substantive requirements
for filing a lawsuit. The court upheld the dismissal of such lawsuit. Based on the ruling of the above,
our PRC Legal Advisers are of the view that the pending litigation lodged by Jinshun Mining against
Huaxia Mining will not have any significant impacts on our business operations and financial
performance, given that the amount involved in this case accounts for only 0.99% of the Group’s net
asset value as at 31 July 2025, and that the legal representative of Jinshun Mining has previously filed
multiple lawsuits based on the same facts under the said service agreement at issue, all of which
lacked a substantive factual basis and thus have been dismissed.
RISK MANAGEMENT AND INTERNAL CONTROL
Risk Management and Corporate Governance
In the regular progression of our business activities, we are inherently subject to a spectrum of
risks, encompassing market, operational and financial risks. It is through this lens that we approach
risk mitigation, ensuring that our business operations are safeguarded against potential adversities,
thereby securing our competitive edge and business and financial stability. Accordingly, we have
established a risk management system with relevant policies and procedures that we believe are
appropriate for our business operations. We have adopted and implemented comprehensive risk
− 251 −

=== PAGE 262 ===
BUSINESS
management policies in various aspects of our business operations, such as financial reporting,
compliance, and anti-bribery. Such risk management policies are established by our Board and are
updated from time to time, based on the current effective PRC laws and regulations and our Articles.
Our conviction stands firm that the existing internal control mechanism and procedures will epitomise
adequacy of our operational effectiveness. To monitor the ongoing implementation of our risk
management policies and corporate governance measures after Listing, we have adopted, and will
continue to put in place the following risk management measures:
(a) Code of Conduct: Our code of conduct explicitly communicates to each employee our
values, acceptable criteria for decision-making and our ground rules for behaviour.
(b) Internal Audit: Our internal audit function regularly monitors key controls and procedures
in order to assure our management and Board that the internal control system is functioning
as intended. The Audit Committee of our Board is responsible for supervising our internal
audit function.
(c) Licensing: In accordance with our internal measures, our Audit and Legal Department is
assigned to ensure we have all necessary licences for our business operation and to keep
track of the licensing update and renewal.
(d) Compliance with Listing Rules and PRC Laws: We will continue to monitor our
compliance with relevant laws and regulations and our senior management team will work
closely with our employees to implement actions required to ensure our compliance with
relevant laws and regulations. We will also continue to arrange various trainings to be
provided by Hong Kong legal advisers to our Directors, senior management and employees
on the Listing Rules, including but not limited to aspects related to corporate governance
and connected transactions, and by our PRC Legal Advisers on PRC laws and regulations.
Our senior management, internal audit and the Audit Committee together monitor the
implementation of our internal control system on an ongoing basis to ensure our policies
and implementation are effective and sufficient.
(e) Investment and Acquisition: We have established an Investment and Acquisition
Department, which is responsible for overseeing all investment activities in accordance
with our pre-established investment management policies and procedures, since February
2025. Under these internal control measures, the total annual investment budget must be
reviewed and approved in advance by our Board, while any major capital investments,
which is defined as a single transaction or a series of related transactions exceeding
RMB50.0 million in aggregate, require specific, case-by-case approval from our Board
following the initial approval of the annual budget.

Internal Control
In preparation for the Listing, we have engaged an independent third party consultant (“Internal
Control Consultant”) to perform a review over selected areas of our internal controls in November
2024 (“Internal Control Review”). The scope of the Internal Control Review performed by the
Internal Control Consultant was agreed between the Internal Control Consultant and us. The selected
areas of our internal controls that have been reviewed by the Internal Control Consultant including
controls environment, risk management, monitoring, information and communication, and anti-money
laundering and anti-fraud programmes under entity level, as well as financial reporting and disclosure,
revenue, purchasing, production/mining, inventory, cash management and treasury, human resources
and payroll, fixed assets & intangible assets, construction in progress, information technology general
control, taxes, insurance, intellectual property under process level. There are other risks relating to
our business and operations and market risks in the ordinary course of our business. See “Risk
Factors” and “Financial Information — Key Factors Affecting Our Results of Operations” in this
prospectus for details. We have subsequently taken corrective actions in response to such findings and
recommendations from our Internal Control Consultant. The Internal Control Consultant performed a
follow-up review in March and April 2025 (“Follow-up Review”) to review the status of the
management actions taken by us to address the findings of the Internal Control Review. The Internal
Control Consultant did not see the need to make any further recommendations in such Follow-up
Review. The Internal Control Review and the Follow-up Review were conducted based on information
provided by us and no assurance or opinion on internal controls was expressed by the Internal Control
Consultant.
Based on the above, our Directors are of the view that our Group has taken reasonable steps to
establish a proper internal control system to minimise risks of non-compliance incidents and prevent
occurrence of non-compliance incidents in future, at both working and monitoring levels. Therefore,
our Directors are of the view that the enhanced internal control measures adopted our Group are
adequate and effective in reducing the risk of future non-compliance incidents by our Group with legal
and regulatory requirements.
COVID-19 IMPACT
During the period of the corona virus disease 2019 (“COVID-19”) pandemic, we swiftly
implemented effective health and safety prevention and proactive response measures to protect our
employees and maintain production. The impact of COVID-19 is low in Xizang. The low population
density in Xizang and on our mining site may be relevant. Throughout the pandemic, the Group did
not experience any significant interruptions or delays in mining or processing activities, or in
transportation of supplies as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic. Our production and transportation
activities required minimal personnel interaction, thereby minimizing the impact of the pandemic on
production. Our Directors confirmed that the COVID-19 pandemic had no material adverse impact on
our business operations and financial performance during theTrack Record Period and up to the Latest
Practical Date.

INDEPENDENCE FROM OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
On the basis of the following factors, our Directors are satisfied that our Group is capable of
carrying on our business independently of our Controlling Shareholders and their respective close
associates after the Listing.
Management Independence
Our daily operational and management decisions are made by our executive Director and our
senior management, with our Board having an overall supervision of our management. Upon the
Listing, our Board will consist of eight Directors comprising one executive Director, four
non-executive Directors and three independent non-executive Directors. For more information, see
“Directors and Senior Management” in this prospectus.
We believe that our Directors and senior management are able to perform their roles in our
Company independently and our Company is capable of managing its business independently from our
Controlling Shareholders and their respective close associates for the following reasons:
(i) each of our Directors is aware of his/her fiduciary duties as a Director which require,
among other things, that he/she acts for the benefit and in the best interests of our Company
and does not allow his/her personal interest to interfere with our best interests;
(ii) in the event that there is a potential conflict of interest arising out of any transaction to be
entered into between our Group and our Directors or their respective close associates, the
interested Director(s) shall abstain from voting on any resolutions of our Board of
Directors approving any contract, arrangement or any other proposal in which he or any of
his/her close associates has a material interest and shall not be counted in the quorum
present at the relevant meeting of our Board of Directors meeting;
(iii) our daily management and operations are carried out by our executive Director, Ms. He,
and our senior management team (in particular Mr. Ma Ying), who have the adequate
relevant experience to ensure the normal operation of the day-to-day business and
management of our Group. Although Ms. He is a party to the AIC Confirmation pursuant
to which parties confirmed that Ms. Fan and Mr. Lv have been the de facto controllers of
our Company and Ms. He has been acting in concert, Ms. Fan and Mr. Lv make decisions
at strategic level of our development and do not involve in our daily management and
operations. As at the Latest Practicable Date, none of the members of our senior
management team held any equity interest in our Controlling Shareholders or their close
associates;
(iv) other than Ms. He, our Directors do not participate in the day-to-day management and
operations of our business. However, they would keep up to date with our business affairs,
provide strategic advice for our business development and assist in supervising and
scrutinising our business performance to fulfil their obligation as a Director. In particular,
the Strategy Committee chaired by Ms. Fan (members consisting of Ms. Fan, Mr. Lv and

(v) we have appointed three independent non-executive Directors, comprising over one-third

Operational Independence
Our Group is operationally independent of our Controlling Shareholders and their respective
close associates. We can make decisions and carry out our own business operations independently. We
have sufficient capital, facilities, technology and employees to operate our business independently.
We hold or enjoy the benefits of all relevant licences and intellectual properties necessary to operate
our business. We own or have the right to use all the operational facilities relating to our business.
We have our own organisational structure made up of individual functional departments, each with
specific areas of responsibilities.
We have not shared any operational resources such as sales and marketing, risk management and
general administration resources with our Controlling Shareholders or their respective close
associates. We have also established a set of internal control procedures to facilitate the effective
operation of our business. We independently manage and have independent access to our customers
and suppliers. In the event that any conflict of interest arises between our Group and the Controlling
Shareholders, our independent non-executive Directors will also provide checks and balances over the
decisions of our Board on significant transactions, connected transactions and other transactions
involving any actual or potential conflict of interests.

RELATIONSHIP WITH OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
Financial Independence
Our Group has an independent financial system and makes financial decisions according to our
own business needs.We have our own internal control and accounting systems and finance department
to perform independent treasury function on cash receipts and payments, independent accounting and
reporting functions and independent internal control function. Neither our Controlling Shareholders
nor their respective close associates intervene with our use of funds. We have adequate internal
resources and credit profile to support our daily operations, and we are capable of obtaining financing
from independent third parties without relying on any guarantee or security provided by our
Controlling Shareholders or their respective close associates.As at the Latest Practicable Date, we did
not have any outstanding borrowing or guarantee from our Controlling Shareholders or any of their
respective close associates.
Based on the above, our Directors are of the view that we are able to maintain financial
independence from our Controlling Shareholders and their respective close associates.
BUSINESS DELINEATION AND COMPETITION
We are a mining company focused on lead and zinc exploration, mining, production and sales
of concentrates based in Xizang, China. We have a comprehensive business operation chain that
encompasses exploration, mining, production, and sales of concentrates. For further details of our
business, see “Business” in this prospectus.
Rule 8.10 of the Listing Rules
As at the Latest Practicable Date, none of our Controlling Shareholders or Directors had any
interest in any business which competes or is likely to compete, either directly or indirectly, with our
business which would require disclosure under Rule 8.10 of the Listing Rules.
Xizang Shengyuan
Notwithstanding the fact that our Company was held as to 44.28% by Xizang Shengyuan as at
the Latest Practicable Date, we consider Xizang Shengyuan is a financial investor with a passive role
and Xizang Shengyuan has no involvement in our day-to-day operations and management. Xizang
Shengyuan, being a wholly owned enterprise by Xizang SASAC, was established as a state-owned
investment holding entity. Among eight Directors on the Board of our Company, two Directors were
nominated by Xizang Shengyuan. To the best knowledge of our Company and as confirmed by Xizang
Shengyuan, the Director nominated by Xizang Shengyuan is not involved in the day-to-day operations
and management of our Company.
− 258 −

=== PAGE 269 ===
RELATIONSHIP WITH OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
The principal business of Xizang Shengyuan does not compete, or is likely to compete, either
directly or indirectly, with our business and would require disclosure under Rule 8.10 of the Listing
Rules. We are a mining company focusing our business on zinc, lead and copper exploration, mining,
production and sales of concentrates. In contrast, the principal business of Xizang Shengyuan is
investment holding of mining companies in Xizang on behalf of Xizang Government and Xizang
Shengyuan does not operate these mining companies. Furthermore, there is no competition, or likely
to be any competition, either directly or indirectly, between the companies that Xizang Shengyuan
invested in and companies in our Group. Among all the companies that Xizang Shengyuan holds
interests in, none of them operate business in relation to the production of zinc and lead. For those
companies that Xizang Shenyuan can consolidate their financial results, they may have exploration
rights but do not possess mining rights. For those companies that do have mining rights or are engaged
in production of minerals, Xizang Shengyuan does not consolidate the financial results of any of them.
Therefore, there is no competition between the business of Xizang Shengyuan and that of our Group.
Xizang Zhifeng
We consider that there is clear delineation of our principal business from the business of our
Controlling Shareholders. One of the Controlling Shareholders, Xizang Zhifeng, is an investment
holding vehicle with no business other than holding the interests in our Company. None of Ms. Fan,
Mr. Lv and Ms. He has any interest in any business which competes or is likely to compete, either
directly or indirectly, with our principal business.
Zhihui Partnership
We consider that there is clear delineation of our principal business from the business of our
Controlling Shareholders. One of the Controlling Shareholders, Zhihui Partnership, purely operates as
our employee shareholding platform, which has or will have no interest in any business which
competes or is likely to compete, either directly or indirectly, with our principal business.
NON-COMPETITION UNDERTAKING
In light of the managerial roles of Xizang Zhifeng’s shareholders in our Company, Xizang
Zhifeng, Ms. Fan, Mr. Lv and Ms. He (the “Covenantors”) have irrevocably and unconditionally
undertaken to us in the Deed of Non-competition (for itself and as trustee for its subsidiaries) that they
will not, and will procure that none of their respective associates (other than members of our Group)
will, during the Restricted Period (as defined below), directly or indirectly, either on their own
account, in conjunction with, on behalf of, or through any person, firm or company, among other
things, carry on, participate or be interested, engaged or otherwise involved in or acquire or hold (in
each case whether as a shareholder, partner, agent or otherwise and whether for profit, reward or
otherwise) the zinc, lead and copper mining related operations, including geological exploration and
mining, processing, smelting and technical services, and production and sales of specialised
equipment and supplies and construction materials for zinc, lead and copper mines and/or any other
new business that we may undertake from time to time after the Listing within the PRC (collectively
referred to as “Restricted Business“) and where they become aware of such engagement of the
Restricted Business they shall notify our Company forthwith.
− 259 −

=== PAGE 270 ===
RELATIONSHIP WITH OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
The above restriction does not apply to the Covenantors with respect to their interests in the
shares of any member of our Group, or interests in the shares of a company (other than our Group)
which are listed on a recognised stock exchange provided that (i) the total number of the shares held
by any the Covenantors and/or her/his/its associates (in aggregate) does not amount to more than 5%
of the issued shares of such company; and (ii) any of the Covenantors and/or his/her/its associates are
not entitled to nominate a majority of the directors of that company.
Further, each of the Covenantors has undertaken that if any business investment/other
commercial opportunity relating to the Restricted Businesses (the “Competing Business
Opportunity“) is identified by or offered to it or any of its close associates (other than members of
our Group), it shall, and shall procure that its close associates shall, refer such Competing Business
Opportunity to our Company on a timely basis by giving written notice (the “Offer Notice“)
containing all information reasonably necessary for our Company to consider whether to pursue such
Competing Business Opportunity.
Upon receiving the Offer Notice, we shall seek opinions and decisions from a Board committee
who do not have an interest in the Competing Business Opportunity (the “Independent Board“) as
to whether to pursue or decline the Competing Business Opportunity. Such Covenantor shall be
entitled to pursue such Competing Business Opportunity only if (i) it has received a written notice
from our Company declining the Competing Business Opportunity and confirming that the Competing
Business Opportunity would not constitute competition with the Restricted Business, or (ii) it has not
received the notice from our Company within ten (10) Business Days from the receipt of the Offer
Notice by our Company. If there is any material change in the nature, terms or conditions of such
Competing Business Opportunity pursued by the Covenantor, it shall refer such revised Competing
Business Opportunity to our Company as if it were a new Competing Business Opportunity.
In the event that any of the Covenantors and/or his/her/its associates (other than our Group)
wishes to dispose of his/her/its business investment or interest in any entity relating to the Restricted
Business he/she/it have acquired, such Covenantor and/or his/her/its associates (other than our Group)
shall provide our Group with pre-emptive right (“Pre-emptive Right“) to acquire any such interest
in the Restricted Business under the same circumstances. Where the relevant committee of our Board
of Directors decides to waive the Pre-emptive Right by way of written notice, such Covenantor and/or
his/her/its associates (other than our Group) may offer to sell such business investment or interest in
the Restricted Business to other third parties on such terms which are no more favourable than those
made available to our Group. In deciding whether to exercise the above Pre-emptive Right, our
Directors will consider various factors including the purchase price and their values and benefits, as
well as the benefit that they will bring to our Group.
The Covenantors have further undertaken to us that it will provide and procure its close
associates to provide on best endeavour basis, all information necessary for the annual review by our
independent non-executive Directors for the enforcement of the Deed of Non-competition. They will
make a written confirmation in our annual report on the compliance with the Deed of
Non-competition.

RELATIONSHIP WITH OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
Each of the Covenantors acknowledges and agrees that our Directors who have no material
interest in the matters discussed will/may, based on the information available to them, including
information and confirmation provided by or obtained from such Covenantor and/or his/her/its

The obligation of the Covenantors under the Deed of Non-competition shall continue during the

jointly, are entitled to exercise, or control the exercise of, not less than the 30% of the voting power
at general meetings of our Company, or control the composition of a majority of our Board; or (iii)
close associates of the Covenantors remain as a director of any member of our Group.
CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
We will comply with the provisions of the Corporate Governance Code in Appendix C1 to the
Listing Rules, which set out principles of good corporate governance. Our Directors recognise the
importance of good corporate governance in protection of our Shareholders’interests.We would adopt
the following measures to safeguard good corporate governance standards and to avoid potential
conflict of interests between our Group and the Controlling Shareholders:
(a) where a general meeting is held for considering proposed transactions in which any of our
Controlling Shareholders has a material interest, she/he/it shall abstain from voting on the
relevant resolutions and shall not be counted in the quorum for the voting;
(b) where a Board meeting is held for the matters in which a Director has a material interest,
such Director shall abstain from voting on the relevant resolutions and shall not be counted
in the quorum for the voting;
(c) in the event that our independent non-executive Directors are requested to review any
conflict of interest between our Group and any of our Controlling Shareholders, she/he/it
shall provide the independent non-executive Directors with all necessary information and
our Company shall disclose the decisions of the independent non-executive Directors either
in its annual reports or by way of announcements;
(d) the independent board committee comprising independent non-executive Directors who are
independent of the Covenantors will be responsible for reviewing, considering and
deciding whether to pursue or decline any Competing Business Opportunity referred to by
the Covenantors pursuant to the Deed of Non-competition, and an independent financial
adviser or other professional advisers may be appointed or engaged as the independent
board committee considers necessary to advise them on the terms of such Competing
Business Opportunity;
− 261 −

=== PAGE 272 ===
RELATIONSHIP WITH OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
(e) the independent board committee comprising independent non-executive Directors who are
independent of the Covenantors will decide whether or not to pursue the Competing
Business Opportunity/exercise the Pre-emptive Right. Such independent board committee
may appoint or engage an independent financial adviser or other professional advisers to
advise it. The Covenantors shall provide all information reasonably required by such
independent board committee to assist them in their assessment of the exercise or
non-exercise of the Competing Business Opportunity and/or Pre-emptive Right;
(f) our Directors (including our independent non-executive Directors) will seek independent
and professional opinions from external advisers at our Company’s cost as and when
appropriate in accordance with the Corporate Governance Code and Corporate Governance
Report set out in Appendix C1 to the Listing Rules;
(g) our Directors will receive mandatory director training each year in compliance with the
requirements of the Listing Rules to develop and refresh their knowledge and skills to keep
pace with continuous regulatory developments; and
(h) we have appointed Maxa Capital Limited, with effect upon the Listing, as our Compliance
Adviser who will provide us with professional advice and guidance, in respect of
compliance with the Listing Rules and applicable laws including various requirements
relating to directors’ duties and corporate governance.
Based on above, our Directors are satisfied that sufficient corporate governance measures have
been put in place to manage conflicts of interest between our Group and our Controlling Shareholders
and/or other Directors to protect minority Shareholders’ rights after the Listing.

DIRECTORS AND SENIOR MANAGEMENT
Our Board is of the view that our Board satisfies our Board Diversity Policy. The Nomination
Committee is responsible for reviewing the diversity of our Board, reviewing our Board Diversity
Policy from time to time, developing and reviewing measurable objectives for implementing our
Board Diversity Policy, and monitoring the progress on achieving these measurable objectives in
order to ensure that the policy remains effective. We will (i) disclose the biographical details of each
Director and (ii) report on the implementation of our Board Diversity Policy (including whether we
have achieved board diversity) in its annual corporate governance report. In particular, we will take
opportunities to increase the proportion of female members of our Board when selecting and
recommending suitable candidates for our Board appointments to help enhance gender diversity in
accordance with stakeholder expectations and recommended best practices.
Four out of eight of our Directors upon Listing are female, and we have been taking and will
continue to take steps to maintain that our Board with gender diversity. Further, we have been taking,
and will continue to take steps to promote gender diversity at our Board and management levels. Our
Board Diversity Policy provides that our Board should aim to maintain the proportion of female
members over time after the Global Offering where possible when selecting and making
recommendations on suitable candidates for our Board appointments. We place great importance on
gender diversity, with approximately 10.6% of our employees being female as at 31 July 2025.We will
(i) aim to maintain the percentage of female staff who has the necessary skills and experience,
especially at middle to senior level; (ii) provide career development and training opportunities to our
female staff whom we consider having the suitable experience, skill and knowledge of our operation
and business to prepare them with the required attributes and competencies to serve as members of
our Board with regards to our strategic needs and the industry in which we operate, such that they will
be eligible for managerial and board-level positions in the future; and (iii) identify and select suitable
female candidates to become our Board members and such candidates will be reviewed and
recommended by our nomination committee to our Board periodically. We are of the view that the
above measures will offer greater prospects for securing a pipeline of female candidates to maintain
gender diversity in our Board in the long run.
In addition, two out of eight of our Directors are Zang ethnic minority. We have achieved ethnic
diversity within our leadership, which enables us to gain deeper insights into Xizang’s unique culture.
Our workforce reflects the rich ethnic inclusion and our employees are from Han and Zang, Mongol,
Manchu, Hui, Tujia, Yi, and Pumi ethnic minorities, with Zang ethnic employees account for 15.8%
of our employees as at 31 July 2025. This ethnic inclusion is a point of pride for our Company, as it
creates a dynamic and inclusive work environment that draws from a wide range of perspectives and
life experiences. We actively promote cross-cultural understanding and collaboration, enabling
employees of all ethnic backgrounds to contribute their unique talents and skills.

THE CORNERSTONE PLACING
We have entered into cornerstone investment agreements (each a “Cornerstone Investment
Agreement”, and together the “Cornerstone Investment Agreements”) with the cornerstone
investors set out below (each a “Cornerstone Investor”, and together the “Cornerstone Investors”),
pursuant to which the Cornerstone Investors have agreed to, subject to certain conditions, subscribe,
or cause their designated entities to subscribe, at the Offer Price for such number of Offer Shares
(rounded down to the nearest whole board lot of 1,000 Shares) that may be purchased for an aggregate
amount of approximately HK$224.32 million based on an Offer Price of HK$4.51(being the maximum
Offer Price) and exclusive of brokerage fee, the SFC transaction levy, theAFRC transaction levy and
the Stock Exchange trading fee) (the “Placing”).
Based on the Offer Price of HK$4.51, being the maximum of the indicated Offer Price range, the
total number of Offer Shares to be subscribed by the Cornerstone Investors would be 49,737,000
Shares, representing approximately (i) 40.78% of the Offer Shares offered pursuant to the Global
Offering, and (ii) 10.19% of our total issued share capital immediately upon completion of the Global
Offering.
Based on the Offer Price of HK$4.30, being the mid-point of the indicated Offer Price range, the
total number of Offer Shares to be subscribed by the Cornerstone Investors would be 50,603,000
Shares, representing approximately (i) 41.50% of the Offer Shares offered pursuant to the Global
Offering, and (ii) 10.37% of our total issued share capital immediately upon completion of the Global
Offering.
Based on the Offer Price of HK$4.10, being the minimum of the indicated Offer Price range, the
total number of Offer Shares to be subscribed by the Cornerstone Investors would be 51,512,000
Shares, representing approximately (i) 42.24% of the Offer Shares offered pursuant to the Global
Offering, and (ii) 10.56% of our total issued share capital immediately upon completion of the Global
Offering.
Our Company is of the view that, (i) the Cornerstone Placing will ensure a reasonable size of
solid commitment at the beginning of the marketing period of the Global Offering and will provide
confidence to the market; and (ii) given the background of the Cornerstone Investors, the Cornerstone
Placing will help raise the profile of our Company and to signify that such investor has confidence
in our business and prospect. We became acquainted with each of the Cornerstone Investors in its
ordinary course of operation through our Group’s business network, or through introduction by our
Company’s business partners or the Overall Coordinators of the Global Offering.
The Cornerstone Investors will acquire the Offer Shares pursuant to, and as part of, the
International Offering. The Cornerstone Investors has agreed that the relevant Offer Shares that it will
subscribe will be fully paid before the Listing. There will be no delayed delivery nor delayed
settlement in respect of Offer Shares to the Cornerstone Investors. The Offer Shares to be subscribed
by the Cornerstone Investors will rank pari passu in all respects with the other fully paid Shares in
issue and will be counted towards the public float of our Company under Rule 8.08 of the Listing
Rules.

SHARES OF OUR COMPANY
The H Shares, to be issued following the completion of the Global Offering, and the Domestic
Shares are ordinary Shares in the share capital of our Company, all of which are considered as one
class of Shares. H Shares may only be subscribed for and traded in Hong Kong dollars. Domestic
Shares and H Shares are regarded as one class of Shares under our Articles of Association and will
rank pari passu with each other in all other respects and, in particular, will rank equally for all
dividends or distributions declared, paid or made after the date of this prospectus. Dividends in
respect of our Shares may be paid by us in Hong Kong dollars or Renminbi, as the case may be. In
addition to cash, dividends may be distributed in the form of Shares.
CONVERSION OF OUR DOMESTIC SHARES INTO H SHARES
According to the regulations by the securities regulatory authorities of the State Council and our
Articles of Association, the Domestic Shares may be converted into H Shares, and such converted
Shares may be listed and traded on an overseas stock exchange provided that the conversion, listing
and trading of such converted Shares have been approved by the securities regulatory authorities of
the State Council. In addition, such conversion, trading and listing shall complete any requisite
internal approval process and in all respects comply with the regulations prescribed by the securities
regulatory authorities of the State Council and the regulations, requirements and procedures
prescribed by the relevant overseas stock exchange.

SHARE CAPITAL
Based on the procedures for the conversion of our Domestic Shares into H Shares as described
in this section, we can apply for the listing of all or any portion of our Domestic Shares on the Stock
Exchange as H Shares in advance of any proposed conversion to ensure that the conversion process
can be completed promptly upon notice to the Stock Exchange and delivery of Shares for entry on the
H Share register. As any listing of additional Shares after our Listing on the Stock Exchange is
ordinarily considered by the Stock Exchange to be a purely administrative matter, it does not require
such prior application for listing at the time of our Listing in Hong Kong.
No voting by class Shareholders is required for the listing and trading of the converted Shares

after our initial listing is subject to prior notification by way of announcement to inform Shareholders
and the public of any proposed transfer.
So far as we are aware, none of our Shareholders currently proposes to convert any of their
Domestic Shares into H Shares.
RESTRICTION OF SHARE TRANSFER
In accordance with the PRC Company Law, the shares issued prior to any public offering of
shares by a company cannot be transferred within one year from the date on which such publicly
offered shares are listed and traded on the relevant stock exchange. As such, the Shares issued by our
Company prior to the issue of H Shares will be subject to such statutory restriction on transfer within
a period of one year from the Listing Date.
Our Directors and members of the senior management of our Company shall declare their
shareholdings in our Company and any changes in their shareholdings. Shares transferred by our
Directors and members of the senior management each year during their term of office shall not
exceed 25% of their total respective shareholdings in our Company. The Shares that the
aforementioned persons held in our Company cannot be transferred within one year from the date on
which the shares are listed and traded, nor within half a year after they leave their positions in our
Company. TheArticles ofAssociation may contain other restrictions on the transfer of the Shares held
by our Directors and members of senior management of our Company.

of 2022, 2023 and 2024 refer to the years ended 31 December of each of 2022, 2023 and 2024. In
addition, the following discussion and analysis contains certain amounts and percentage figures
that have been subject to rounding adjustments, Accordingly, figures shown as totals in certain
tables may not be arithmetic aggregation of the figures preceding them, and all monetary amounts
and percentages shown are approximate amounts only.
OVERVIEW
We are a mining company focusing our business on zinc, lead and copper exploration, mining,
production and sales of concentrates based in Xizang, China. Our mining operations are located in
Rongdoi Township, Jiali County, Nagqu, Xizang. Our Mengya’a Mine comprises an open-pit mine,
which has been in commercial operation since 2007, and an underground mine, which has commenced
commercial operation since the second quarter of 2025. Our mining operations are located within the
nationally designated Jinda Integrated ExplorationArea at an altitude between 5,000.0 and 5,300.0 m
asl. We hold exploration rights over an area of approximately 58.5 sq.km and mining rights over an
area of approximately 4.5 sq.km. According to SMM, we ranked fifth in terms of the annual
production volume of zinc concentrates, fourth in terms of the annual production volume of lead
concentrates, and fifth in terms of the annual production volume of copper concentrates in Xizang in
2024.
We have a business operation chain that encompasses exploration, mining, production and sales
of concentrates. Our main products include zinc concentrates, lead concentrates and copper
concentrates. During the Track Record Period, our customers consisted of (i) nonferrous metal traders
who generally conducted onward sales to end users of zinc, lead and copper concentrates and (ii)
refineries which further processed our concentrates based on the needs of their customers.
For the years ended 31 December 2022, 2023, 2024 and the seven months ended 31 July 2025,
our total revenue was approximately RMB482.4 million, RMB546.1 million, RMB301.4 million and
RMB256.6 million, respectively. Our gross profit was approximately RMB174.6 million, RMB217.7
million, RMB104.5 million and RMB85.7 million, with a gross profit margin of approximately 36.2%,
39.9%, 34.7% and 33.4%, respectively. Our net profit was approximately RMB117.9 million,
RMB154.7 million, RMB55.9 million and RMB51.7 million, respectively. For the same years/period,
our net profit margin was approximately 24.4%, 28.3%, 18.5% and 20.2%, respectively.

KEY FACTORS AFFECTING OUR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Our results of operations and financial position have been and will continue to be affected by
a number of factors, including those set out in “Risk Factors” in this prospectus and those discussed
below:
Changes in demand for our concentrates may affect the price of our concentrates
Zinc, lead and copper are major global and domestic commodities whose prices are influenced
by a variety of complex factors. One significant factor is the state of the global economy. For instance,
during economic downturns, industrial activity declines, leading to reduced demand for these metals
and subsequent price drops. Conversely, in periods of economic growth, especially with the rapid
development of emerging economies like China, demand for these metals can rise significantly,
driving selling prices up. Additionally, changes in supply and demand dynamics are crucial in
determining prices. If major producing countries experience supply shortages due to natural disasters
or labour disputes, this could lead to market tightness and increase in prices. On the contrary,
weakened demand or increased supply from new mines may cause prices to fall.
It is important for us to understand these market dynamics, and we have established a
comprehensive price monitoring and analysis system to obtain timely market information and adjust
concentrate production and sales strategies accordingly. For example, if metal prices are expected to
rise in the near future, increasing inventory could be beneficial to sell at higher prices later. By
contrast, if prices are projected to decline, accelerating sales would be wise to avoid losses from
excess inventory.
Our reserves and processing capability of our Mengya’a Beneficiation Plant
The reserves of our Mengya’a Mine and the capability of the processing plant directly influence
our long-term production capabilities and economic performance. Accurate geological exploration
and resource assessment ensure the reliability of reserve data, allowing for the development of a
sound long-term production plan. High-grade ores typically lead to greater economic benefits, but
mineralised waste, by virtue of comprehensive utilisation, can also be economically extracted through
optimised processing techniques. The daily processing capability of the processing plant and the
sophistication of its equipment determine the yield of concentrates. Modern processing facilities and
− 293 −

=== PAGE 304 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
automated control systems can significantly enhance processing capability and recovery rates, reduce
waste generation and improve overall production efficiency. Furthermore, continuously optimising the
processing workflow, by employing advanced flotation technologies and effectively managing tailings
to recover residual value, is essential for increasing both the quantity and quality of our concentrates.
Our ability to adapt business operations to local conditions and culture of Xizang
Conducting business in a unique environment requires a deep understanding of local conditions
and cultural contexts. Therefore, it is essential for us to adapt our business operations to the specific
characteristics of Xizang, respecting the rich cultural heritage and customs that shape the local
community.
We shall respect and integrate local practices into our business strategies and foster strong
relationships and build trust within the local community such that we can enhance our operational
success. Being sensitive to the unique cultural and environmental aspects of Xizang allows us to
operate more effectively. This adaptability is key for us to navigating challenges and seizing
opportunities that align with the local values and needs, ultimately driving sustainable growth for our
business in the region.
Logistics transportation and supply chain management
Due to Xizang’s remote geographical location and challenging transportation conditions, the
costs of raw material supply, subcontracting arrangement and transportation are relatively high.
Effective supply chain management, subcontracting management and logistics optimisation are
crucial for controlling costs. Establishing an efficient logistics network, engaging competent and
qualified subcontractors, selecting appropriate transportation methods, and utilising information
technology to enhance supply chain transparency and responsiveness are key measures to reduce
unnecessary costs and improve customer satisfaction. For instance, rationally planning transportation
routes and choosing the most economical transportation methods can significantly lower logistics
expenses.
Our ability to continuously promote technological upgrades and innovations
We render ongoing technological innovation and investment in R&D to enhance our
competitiveness and profitability. Implementing more efficient mining and processing technologies
creates advanced management systems that improve production efficiency and real-time monitoring
and scheduling capabilities. The application of green mining technologies is increasingly important,
as they help reduce environmental pollution during extraction and processing, ensuring our
compliance with strict environmental regulations. Additionally, continuous R&D investment can lead
to the discovery of new minerals or improved utilisation of existing ones, such as extracting more
valuable metals from mineralised waste.
− 294 −

=== PAGE 305 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Our mining operations are subject to seasonality primarily because of the unique weather
conditions of Xizang
The unique weather conditions of Xizang significantly impact our mining operations and
financial performance. The region’s plateau climate features substantial temperature variations and
distinct rainy and dry seasons. Summer (June to August) is the optimal period for exploration and
mining due to milder temperatures, enhancing workers’productivity. However, this season also brings
heavy rainfall, sleet and hail, which can lead to slippery roads and mudslides, necessitating
precautionary measures for safe logistics. Conversely, winter (November to March or April) presents
extreme cold, with freezing conditions that complicate extraction efforts and increase operational
costs. These weather-related challenges require our careful planning to optimise our mining
operations and manage risks effectively throughout the year.
Changes in government policies and regulations with respect to the region and the industry
Changes in government policies and regulations, including tax incentives and environmental
protection requirements, may have an impact on our Group. This is particularly important in
ecologically sensitive areas including Xizang, where adherence to strict environmental regulations is
of great importance. For instance, tax reductions and other financial incentives provided by the local
government can directly lower our operating costs and improve our profit margin.
In addition to economic support, governments also regulate mining activities through legislation
to ensure compliance with environmental protection standards. In fragile ecological regions like
Xizang, improper development practices can lead to severe consequences. Therefore, strictly adhering
to local environmental regulations and implementing high standards of ecological protection measures
is not only a legal requirement but also a reflection of social responsibility. Examples include
adopting advanced tailings treatment technologies to minimise water and soil pollution, and
conducting vegetation restoration projects to promote the recovery of ecosystems around mining
areas. Furthermore, actively participating in local community development projects, such as
improving infrastructure and providing employment opportunities, can enhance our influence in the
region as business operations in the region require seamless adoption to the local unique
circumstances.

Income Tax Expense
We are subject to Enterprise Income Tax (“EIT”) in China, which requires significant judgment
in determining the appropriate provision for EIT. According to the Notice of the Continuation of the
Enterprise Income Tax for Implementation of Exploration and Development of Western Region 《( 關
於延續西部大開發企業所得稅政策的公告》) (Notice of the Ministry of Finance, StateAdministration
of Taxation and National Development and Reform Commission No. 23 [2020]) issued on 23 April
2020, companies located in the western region of the PRC and engaged in the business encouraged
by the PRC Government is entitled to the preferential EIT rate of 15% from 1 January 2021 to 31
December 2030 if the operating revenue of the encouraged business in a year accounted for more than
60% of the total income in that year. We are engaged in the “business encouraged by the PRC
Government in the western region” and hence become eligible for the preferential EIT rate at 15%
during the Track Record Period. During the normal course of our business, there are various
transactions and calculations in which the ultimate tax determination may be uncertain. If the final
tax outcomes differ from the amounts initially recorded, these differences will affect both our current
income tax and deferred tax provisions in the period when the determinations are made. This inherent
uncertainty underscores the importance of our accounting policies and estimates related to income tax,
which are critical for accurately reflecting our financial position and performance.
Estimation Uncertainty
In the application of our accounting policies, our management is required to make judgements,
estimates and assumptions about the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities that are not readily
apparent from other sources. These estimates and associated assumptions are based on historical
experience and other factors that are considered to be relevant. Actual results may differ from these
estimates. These estimates and underlying assumptions are reviewed on an ongoing basis. Revisions
to accounting estimates are recognised in the period in which the estimates are revised if the revision
affects only that period, or in the period of the revision and future periods if the revision affects both
current and future periods.
Ore reserves
Technical estimates of our ore reserves are inherently imprecise and represent only approximate
amounts because of the subjective judgements employed in developing such information. There are
authoritative guidelines regarding the engineering criteria that have to be satisfied before estimated
ore reserves can be designated as “proved” and “probable”. Proved and probable ore reserves
estimates are updated on a regular basis upon taking into account the recent economic production and
technical information of each mine. In addition, as production levels and technical standards change
from year to year, the estimate of proved and probable ore reserves also changes. Despite the inherent
− 296 −

=== PAGE 307 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
imprecision in these technical estimates, these estimates are used in determining the depreciation of
certain property, plant and equipment and amortisation for mining rights. Details of these property,
plant and equipment and mining rights are set out in notes 15 and 17 of the Accountants’ Report in
Appendix I to this prospectus.
Asset retirement obligation
The estimation of the liabilities for asset retirement obligation involves estimating of the amount
and timing for the future cash spending as well as the discount rate used for reflecting current market
assessments of the time value of money and the risks specific to the liability. We consider the factors,
including the development plan of the mines, the geological structure of the mining regions and
reserve volume, to determine the scope, amount and timing of retirement obligation to be performed.
Determination of the effect of these factors involves judgements from our Group and the estimated
liabilities may turn out to be different from the actual expenditure to be incurred. The discount rate
used by us may also be altered to reflect the changes in the market assessments of the time value of
money and the risks specific to the liability, such as change of the borrowing rate and inflation rate
in the market. As changes in estimates occur such as mine plan revisions, changes in estimated costs,
or changes in timing of the performance of retirement activities, the revisions to the obligation will
be recognised at the appropriate discount rate. Details of the provisions for asset retirement obligation
are set out in note 30 of the Accountants’ Report in Appendix I to this prospectus.

For the years ended 31 December 2022, 2023, 2024 and the seven months ended 31 July 2025,
our effective tax rate was approximately 12.6%, 11.0%, 11.1% and 9.7%, respectively.
During the Track Record Period, as our Company and all of our operating subsidiaries are
incorporated in the PRC, we are subject to EIT of the PRC on each of our Company and our
subsidiaries’ taxable income in accordance with the EIT Law. According to the EIT Law, a uniform
25% EIT rate is generally applicable to both foreign-invested enterprises and domestic enterprises,
except where a special preferential rate applies. The EIT is calculated based on the entity’s global
income as determined under PRC tax laws and accounting standards.
According to the Notice of the Continuation of the Enterprise Income Tax for Implementation
of Exploration and Development of Western Region 《( 關於延續西部大開發企業所得稅政策的公告》)
(Notice of the Ministry of Finance, State Administration of Taxation and National Development and
Reform Commission No. 23 [2020]) issued on 23 April 2020, companies which are located in the
western region of the PRC and engaged in the business encouraged by the PRC Government is entitled
to the preferential EIT rate of 15% from 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2030 if the revenue of the
encouraged business in a year accounted for more than 60% of the total income in that year. Each of
our Company and Zhihua Industrial was engaged in the “business encouraged by the PRC Government
in the western region”, are eligible for the preferential EIT rate at 15% for the Track Record Period.
In addition, each of our Company and Zhihua Industrial was granted with further waiver of 40% local
tax and resulted in the tax rate being 9% during the Track Record Period. Huaxia Mining was granted
with a waiver of 40% local tax and resulted in the tax rate being 15% during the Track Record Period.

REVIEW OF HISTORICAL RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Year Ended 31 December 2023 Compared to Year Ended 31 December 2022
Revenue
Our revenue increased by approximately RMB63.7 million, or 13.2%, from approximately
RMB482.4 million for the year ended 31 December 2022 to approximately RMB546.1 million for the
year ended 31 December 2023, primarily attributable to an increase in revenue from sales of lead
concentrates and copper concentrates, primarily driven by the increases in both sales volume and the
average selling price of such concentrates. Such increase was partially offset by a decrease in revenue
from the sales of zinc concentrates. Despite our sales volume of zinc concentrates increased from
approximately 19,766.0 tonnes in 2022 to approximately 23,544.0 tonnes in 2023, the average selling
price of zinc concentrates decreased from RMB14,989.0 per tonne to RMB11,628.0 per tonne during
the same year, which resulted in a decrease in our revenue from the sales of zinc concentrates in 2023.
Cost of Sales
Cost of sales increased by approximately RMB20.7 million, or 6.7% from approximately
RMB307.7 million for the year ended 31 December 2022 to approximately RMB328.4 million for the
year ended 31 December 2023, was primarily attributable to an increase in our sales volume of
concentrates. Our sales volume of concentrates increased by approximately 20.0% from
approximately 30,955.0 tonnes for the year ended 31 December 2022 to approximately 37,135.0
tonnes for the year ended 31 December 2023. The growth rate of our cost of sales in 2023 being
significantly lower than that of our sales volume during the same year was primarily due to that (i)
the grade of ores we obtained during our mining process in 2023 was higher as compared to that of
2022 which yielded higher product outputs at lower processing costs; and (ii) the unit cost of
concentrate production decreased with the increased ore mining volume and ore processing volume
in 2023.
Gross Profit and Gross Profit Margin
As a result of the foregoing, our gross profit increased by approximately RMB43.1 million, or
24.7% from approximately RMB174.6 million for the year ended 31 December 2022 to approximately
RMB217.7 million for the year ended 31 December 2023.

Year Ended 31 December 2024 Compared to Year Ended 31 December 2023
Revenue
Our revenue decreased by approximately RMB244.7 million, or 44.8%, from approximately
RMB546.1 million for the year ended 31 December 2023 to approximately RMB301.4 million for the
year ended 31 December 2024. Such decrease was primarily attributable to production line upgrades
and weather-induced delays during the year. In respect of production line upgrades, in 2024, we
undertook a planned, sequential upgrade and interleaved maintenance of two key production lines at
our processing plant from May to October of 2024, maintaining partial operations throughout that
period. These upgrades were essential to enhance processing capabilities and prepare for the
integration of ores from the underground mine, which has commenced commercial operation since the
second quarter of 2025. The technical upgrades involved complex modifications to equipment to
enhance the overall efficiency of the production lines. This required specialised engineering, testing,
and calibration, which extended downtime, aimed at improving yield, product quality, and
environmental compliance. While beneficial in the long term, the implementation phase temporarily
disrupted normal operations. Consequentially, the production of concentrates was not at full capacity,
resulting in reduced processing days of our processing plant. In respect of weather-induced delays,
unfavourable weather conditions, particularly during April 2024, caused unexpected delays in
production activities. These weather disruptions shortened the effective production period and
affected logistics, raw material handling, and plant operations. Weather conditions also affected
transportation of raw materials and finished products, as well as workforce availability and safety,
further compounding operational challenges.
As a result, the total sales volume of the concentrates decreased from approximately 37,135
tonnes for the year ended 31 December 2023 to approximately 16,176 tonnes for the year ended 31
December 2024, notwithstanding the fact that the average selling price increased in 2024.
Cost of Sales
Cost of sales decreased by approximately RMB131.5 million, or 40.0% from approximately
RMB328.4 million for the year ended 31 December 2023 to approximately RMB196.9 million for the
year ended 31 December 2024, which was generally in line with the decrease in our revenue during
the year.
Gross Profit and Gross Profit Margin
As a result of the foregoing, our gross profit decreased by approximately RMB113.2 million, or
52.0% from approximately RMB217.7 million for the year ended 31 December 2023 to approximately
RMB104.5 million for the year ended 31 December 2024.

in 2025. Gross profit margin decreased from approximately 84.5% for the seven months
ended 31 July 2024 to approximately 82.6% for the seven months ended 31 July 2025, as
the silver content within the copper concentrates decreased, giving rise to a lower selling
price of copper concentrates.
Selling and Distribution Expenses
Selling and distribution expenses decreased by approximately RMB0.1 million, or 25.0% from
approximately RMB0.4 million for the seven months ended 31 July 2024 to approximately RMB0.3
million for the seven months ended 31 July 2025. Such decrease was mainly attributable to a decrease
in the staff costs during the period.
General, Administrative and Other Expenses
General, administrative and other expenses decreased by approximately RMB4.9 million, or
14.6% from approximately RMB33.5 million for the seven months ended 31 July 2024 to
approximately RMB28.6 million for the seven months ended 31 July 2025, as we did not incur any
suspension costs during the period since we resumed our business operation timely since April 2025.
Other Income
Other income decreased by approximately RMB4.8 million, or 59.3% from approximately
RMB8.1 million for the seven months ended 31 July 2024 to approximately RMB3.3 million for the
seven months ended 31 July 2025, primarily attributable to a decrease in government grants during
the period.

Our net current liabilities decreased from approximately RMB79.2 million as at 31 December
